title: EPIC Filter Attribute Sourcing
description:
GOAL

Every catalogue-visible product (localhost:3000/products, 700+) carries a real, source-traceable value for each filter facet that applies to its category, so that when the filter UI ships, selecting a facet actually narrows the grid instead of returning nothing or silently hiding itself.

This epic PRODUCES THE DATA. It does not touch the Sanity schema and does not touch the filter UI. Its single output is a normalized handoff dataset that sang-logium-ylz imports.

SCOPE BOUNDARY
- In scope: the facet values in the canonical map only (~15 facets: Wearing style, Back design, Driver type, Connectivity, Connector/plug, Microphone, Noise cancelling, Requires amplifier, Device type, Form factor, Amplification, DAC included, Balanced output, Inputs, Outputs, Accessory type, Connector/termination, Compatibility, plus Category). Closed-vocabulary, a few data points per product.
- Out of scope: schema fields (ylz L1), migration into Sanity (ylz L3/L4), filter UI (sang-logium-agq), tier-2 deferred facets (impedance value, amp power output, cable length, eartip/earpad material, condition, rating), popularity / best-selling data (its own standalone issue).
- Catalogue-visible = appears on /products. Not visible there => out of scope, period.

ACCEPTANCE TESTS
- When I open the coverage report after a brand batch closes, then every catalogue-visible product of that brand shows a value (or an explicit N/A - facet does not apply) for every facet in its category, and every non-N/A value cites a source URL.
- When I spot-check any 20 sourced values against the manufacturer's own spec page, then all 20 match and none is a guessed or inferred value.
- When I check the handoff dataset, then every value is one of the closed-vocabulary options for that facet - zero free-text, zero invented enums.
- When I review the could-not-source queue, then every unresolved facet/product pair is listed explicitly for human decision and nothing in that queue was filled with a placeholder guess.
- When sang-logium-ylz L4 consumes the handoff dataset, then it is a plain import with no further research required.

CHILD LAYERS - strict order, each blocks the next
D0  Per-facet sourcing rubric
D1  Product x facet applicability matrix
D2  Acquire values in brand batches
D3  Unresolved-value human queue
D4  Normalized handoff dataset

RELATED
- sang-logium-agq - EPIC Filters Sorting: the end-user experience (controls, URL, instant updates). Its when-I-click-X-the-grid-narrows tests cannot pass on real data without this epic. Dependency chain: THIS EPIC -> ylz (L1 schema, L3/L4 import, L5 wiring) -> agq (UI).
- sang-logium-ylz - EPIC Filter Sort Data: schema + migration + wiring. This epic ABSORBS AND REPLACES ylz L4 (Fill remaining facet gaps); it can run in parallel with ylz L0-L2 since schema design needs only the canonical map, not the values.

EXECUTION MODEL
Research + structured-data work only. Output is files under _project/filters/ (rubric, worksheet, handoff dataset, coverage report). No schema edits, no Sanity migration runs, no UI, no git, no build/test. The human reviews the dataset and the unresolved queue.

CURRENT STATUS: not started. Draft approved 2026-09-03; canonical facet map lives in _project/scratch/filter-map.html and (authoritatively) in sang-logium-ylz L0.

- _project/filters/sort-map.json — one entry per sort option:

- Two dedicated schema objects on `product`, separate from overviewFields / specifications

  filled for every facet applicable to its category, and a featuredPriority value.
- Chains, one row each:
  facet <-> filterAttributes field <-> URL param <-> query predicate

title: EPIC Filter Sort Data
description:
GOAL

The filter + sort mechanism (its epic `sang-logium-agq` — EPIC Filters Sorting is STALE
and will be re-scoped separately) needs structured data to operate on. Today every product
attribute lives only as free text (overviewFields, specifications, description) and cannot
back a filter, and there is no popularity signal to back a "Best selling" sort. This epic
gives every catalogue-visible product two dedicated, typed groups whose single
responsibility is to power filtering and sorting:

- filterAttributes — one field per facet in the canonical map
- sortAttributes   — featuredPriority + popularity ONLY (price/date sorts keep reading the
                     natural product fields price_data.unit_amount and _createdAt)

Populated by migrating and normalising what already exists, then filling the rest.

SCOPE BOUNDARY

"Catalogue-visible" = appears on localhost:3000/products (700+ products). A product not
visible there is out of scope, period.

ACCEPTANCE TESTS

- When I run the roll-up check after every child layer closes, then it prints: every facet
  AND every sort in the canonical map is wired to its backing field, every catalogue-visible
  product has filterAttributes populated for every facet applicable to its category and a
  featuredPriority value, "closed-vocab violations: 0", "consistency violations: 0".
- When I inspect sanity-cms/schemaTypes/productType.ts, then overviewFields, specifications
  and description are byte-unchanged and filterAttributes + sortAttributes are purely
  additive.
- When I use the filters and the sort control on any category page on :3000, then narrowing
  and reordering reflect the dedicated groups (and price_data / _createdAt for the price and
  date sorts) and no filter or sort path reads a free-text field.

CHILD LAYERS — strict order, each blocks the next

L0  Define end-state + facet/sort map
L1  Add filterAttributes + sortAttributes schema groups
L2  Fresh export + coverage baseline
L3  Migrate + normalize existing fields
L4  Fill remaining facet gaps
L5  Wire filters + sort to the new groups
L6  End-to-end verification

RELATED

- `sang-logium-agq` — EPIC Filters Sorting (mechanism/UI; STALE, to be re-scoped; consumes
  this epic's data)
- "Sorting: populate popularity rank from order history" — standalone, backs the
  "Best selling" sort; depends on L1 (needs sortAttributes.popularity to exist); separate
  cadence, not a migration layer
- `sang-logium-agq.4` — [Filters] Type facet from catalogue subcategories
- `sang-logium-h9j` — Filters: screen cheap product attributes for new facets

CURRENT STATUS: not started. No structured filter data exists; productType.ts carries a
`// TODO Note: Use a different system for Sidebar Filtering.` marker, and `displayPriority`
sits loose on the schema. Latest local product export is ~4 months old (594 docs) and must
be refreshed before any data work.
notes:
RISK ASSESSMENT (added 2026-09-03)

This is an EPIC, not an execution target. No agent implements against this ID — implement
the child layer issues in order.

== A. OUTCOME RISKS ==
A1. Scope bleed between layers (L1 starts writing data, L3 starts wiring UI). MITIGATE:
    every child has its own OUT OF SCOPE + SEQUENCE; a layer that needs the next layer's
    work stops and flags.
A2. Schema designed against the stale 4-month export (594 docs, 436 not in the nav tree).
    MITIGATE: L0/L1 are data-free; L2 forces a fresh export before any data work.
A3. Free text creeping back in as a filter source. MITIGATE: L0 states the one-source
    rule; L5's check asserts no filter path reads overviewFields/specifications/description.
A4. Invented attribute values (hallucinated enums, wrong driver type). MITIGATE: L3 only
    maps values that trace to a real overviewFields entry; L4 values spot-checked against
    manufacturer specs.
A5. Breaking the product-detail display that reads overviewFields. MITIGATE: additive-only
    schema change; existing field blocks byte-unchanged (L1 acceptance test).
A6. Catalogue count drift (700+ live vs whatever an export yields). MITIGATE: L2 reconciles
    export count against localhost:3000/products before the baseline is accepted.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS ==
Lean path = edit source only, hand the CLI + :3000 check to the human.
B1. No build / tsc / lint / test runs.
B2. No agent-run dev server; no browser automation for verification.
B3. No git (branch/commit/push).
B4. No npm install / new deps.
B5. Verification scripts under _project/filters/ are deliverables of L0/L2/L6 — the human

B6. EXCEPTION (L3, L4 only): those layers run Sanity data-migration scripts against the

Expected footprint (whole epic): 1 schema file changed (productType.ts, additive); a
handful of new files under _project/filters/ and sanity-cms migration scripts; filter

UPDATE (2026-09-03): scope extended from filters-only to filters + sorts.

A7. "Best selling" has no data source and could stall the epic. MITIGATE: popularity lives

    (Featured / Price / Newest) never wait on it.
A8. Price or date duplicated into sortAttributes = a second source of truth. MITIGATE:
    sortAttributes holds ONLY featuredPriority + popularity; price/date sorts read
    price_data / _createdAt directly (stated in L0's end-state doc).

title: Pricing: one currency across storefront and checkout
description:
ACCEPTANCE TESTS

This issue starts from an ASSUMPTION (source audit, not yet confirmed on the running app).
Do the diagnostics first and record findings in NOTES before touching any code.

--- Diagnostics / confirmations (do first, record in NOTES) ---

- When I open a product listing page, a product detail page, a homepage product card, the search autocomplete dropdown, the "related products" strip, and an active price-filter chip on localhost:3000, then I record the exact currency symbol and number format each one shows.
- When I add one product to the basket and open the basket, then I record the currency and format on each line item and on the order summary.
- When I go through checkout to the payment step and then the order confirmation page, then I record the currency and format shown; if a receipt email is produced, I record that too.
- When I look at how a product's price is stored in Sanity, then I record whether it carries a currency, and whether the amount is in major units (e.g. 1299) or minor units (e.g. 129900).
- When I confirm with the project owner, then I record the ONE currency and locale the store is intended to use (and whether multi-currency is ever a requirement).

--- Target state (only after the above is confirmed) ---

- When I view a price on any storefront surface (listing, detail, homepage cards, search autocomplete, related products, filter chips), then it shows the same single currency and locale as the basket, checkout, order confirmation and receipt email.
- When the same product's price appears on the storefront and again at checkout, then the number and the currency match exactly.
- When a price has fractional units, then every surface displays it the same way — no surface silently rounds to whole units while another shows decimals.

CURRENT STATUS: not started. Assumption from source audit (_project/audits/intel-BACKLOG.md BL-P0-1; _project/audits/intel-content-copy.md P0-1): app/components/ui/Price.tsx defaults to currency:'USD' / 'en-US' and is called with no currency prop by ProductCard, ProductInfo, IemCard, AccessoryCard; hardcoded '$' also in featured/card/CardDetails.tsx, NewestRelease.tsx, ActiveFilterChips.tsx, AutocompleteItem.tsx, RelatedProducts.tsx. Checkout (CheckoutSummary), account order history, lib/utils/formatting.ts and lib/email.ts format pl-PL / PLN. Not yet confirmed on the running app.
notes:
RISK ASSESSMENT (added 2026-09-03)

This issue is diagnostics-first: the "storefront shows $, checkout shows zł" claim is a
source-audit assumption. Confirm live on :3000 before any edit; if it is already consistent,
close with the recording and do not change code.

== A. OUTCOME RISKS ==
A1. The assumption is wrong or stale — Price.tsx may already be fixed, or a currency prop may be passed higher up. MITIGATE: the diagnostics step confirms live behaviour on :3000 first; if consistent, close as not-a-bug with the recorded evidence.
A2. Wrong currency chosen — the storefront is "fixed" to PLN when the business actually wants USD, or multi-currency. MITIGATE: confirm the intended single currency + locale with the owner before changing anything; record the decision in NOTES.
A3. Scope creep into i18n / multi-currency / FX rates. MITIGATE: this issue is "one currency, shown consistently" — no locale switcher, no FX. If the answer is "we need multi-currency", stop and flag; that is a different issue.
A4. Precision / rounding shift — swapping the formatter reveals .99 endings, or exposes a VAT-inclusive vs exclusive mismatch, or changes displayed totals. MITIGATE: record before/after for a sample of ~10 products across price bands; hand the visual diff to the human.
A5. A price surface is missed — price is formatted in ~8+ call sites. MITIGATE: enumerate every price-rendering call site from the audit PLUS a fresh grep (`Intl.NumberFormat`, `toLocaleString`, `centsToDisplay`, literal `$`) before editing; route all through one shared helper.
A6. Minor vs major unit mismatch — some call sites pass cents, others a decimal amount. MITIGATE: the diagnostics step records the unit each call site passes; the shared helper takes one documented unit and every call site is converted to it.
A7. False "verified" — claiming consistency without the human seeing it. MITIGATE: state what changed; hand the :3000 check (every listed surface + one full add-to-cart → confirmation pass) to the human.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS ==
Lean path = diagnostics by reading source + the human's :3000 recordings; then edit source only (one formatter + its call sites); hand back to :3000.
B1. No build / tsc / ts-check / lint / test.
B2. No agent-run dev server — the human runs :3000 for the diagnostic recordings and the final check.
B3. No browser automation, no Lighthouse, no crawl.
B4. No new deps — `Intl.NumberFormat` is built in.
B5. No git — no branch, commit, or push.
B6. No Sanity / DB writes — the price-schema inspection is read-only.
Escape hatch: if a "no" genuinely blocks the diagnostics (e.g. the owner-confirmation step), stop and say so in one line.
Expected footprint: 1 shared currency formatter (likely consolidating app/components/ui/Price.tsx + lib/utils/formatting.ts) + ~8 call-site edits removing ad-hoc en-US / literal `$` formatting. No schema change, no deps, no config.

IMPLEMENTATION 2026-09-03 (source diagnostics + owner decision + edits)

DIAGNOSTICS (read-only, source; live :3000 recording still owed by human)
- Assumption CONFIRMED at source. Storefront rendered en-US `$`; basket / checkout /
  order confirmation / account orders / receipt email / shipping all rendered pl-PL `zł`/PLN.
- Sanity `price_data`: `unit_amount` = minor units (integer cents); `currency` = string,
  initialValue "usd". Amount is minor units everywhere it is displayed.
- Call sites that passed MAJOR units (dollars) to a formatter: Price.tsx `value`,
  BasketItem `displayPrice`, ShippingPageClient `option.amount`, CardDetails `price`,
  ActiveFilterChips / PriceRangeSlider slider bounds.
- Call sites that passed MINOR units (cents): everything else (CheckoutSummary, OrderDetails,
  success page, account order detail, email, homepage cards, RelatedProducts, AutocompleteItem,
  NewestRelease).

OWNER DECISION (2026-09-03)
- ONE currency + locale: USD / en-US.
- Multi-currency: not a requirement for now. One fixed currency.

CHANGE (source only; no schema, no deps, no git)
- New single formatter in lib/utils/price.ts: `STORE_CURRENCY`/`STORE_LOCALE` +
  `formatPrice(cents)` and `formatPriceMajor(major)` — en-US / USD,
  minimumFractionDigits 0 / maximumFractionDigits 2 (whole -> "$1,299", fractional ->
  "$1,299.99"; no surface rounds a fractional price).
- Price.tsx: drops `currency` and `variant` props, routes through `formatPriceMajor`.
- Routed through the shared helper (removed ad-hoc en-US `$` and pl-PL/PLN formatting):
  ProductCard, ProductInfo, IemCard, AccessoryCard (via Price), RelatedProducts,
  AutocompleteItem, ActiveFilterChips, PriceRangeSlider, NewestRelease, Featured,
  DacCard, CardDetails, BasketItem, BasketSummary, BasketUIMock, CheckoutSummary,
  PaymentForm (Pay button), checkout/success page + OrderDetails,
  account/orders (list + detail), checkout/shipping, lib/email.ts receipt,
  SuccessAnalytics GA4 currency code.
- Deleted `formatPolishPrice` from lib/utils/formatting.ts; updated formatting.test.ts
  and renamed a stale test title in order-summary.test.tsx.

STILL OPEN / FLAGGED (not display; needs owner call)
- Stripe PaymentIntent is created with `currency: 'pln'`
  (app/api/checkout/payment-intent-session/route.ts) and the Klarna
  PaymentMethodMessagingElement (PaymentForm.client.tsx:359) is 'PLN'. Displayed totals
  are now USD but the actual charge currency is still PLN. `pi.amount` is the same integer
  so the confirmation/receipt numbers are consistent, but the money rail currency differs.
- Shipping rate provider data (lib/shipping/carrier-rates.ts, allekurier-rates.ts) carries
  `currency: 'PLN'` and PLN-scale amounts. Not shown directly (amount is formatted as USD),
  but the underlying numbers are Polish-courier priced.
- Polish date locale + Polish UI copy on the shipping step and OrderDetails dates
  (`toLocaleDateString('pl-PL')`, "Wybierz metodę dostawy", etc.) — out of scope here
  (currency only), left as-is.
- Sanity Studio admin previews still show `$` via ad-hoc `/100` (productType.ts,
  orderType.ts) — admin-only, not a storefront surface.

VERIFICATION OWED TO HUMAN (:3000, no automation run)
- Every storefront surface + one full add-to-cart -> shipping -> payment -> confirmation
  pass, plus the receipt email, all showing en-US USD identically.
- No build / tsc / lint / tests were run.

title: [Images] Prove gallery-photo promotion on one product
description:
SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY: Prove the "promote an existing gallery photo to main
image" mechanism end to end on ONE of the 15 products, including that the change
can be undone.

ACCEPTANCE TESTS
- When I open the pilot product on localhost:3000, then its listing card and product page show a sharp photo of that exact product instead of the grey placeholder.
- When I hard-refresh that page with cache disabled, then the correct photo still loads.
- When I look at the other 14 still-broken products and the rest of the catalogue, then nothing else has changed.
- When the change is undone via Sanity document history and I refresh, then the product shows the placeholder again; re-applying restores the photo.

OUT OF SCOPE: the other 14 products; downloading or sourcing any image; deleting
the old 60x45 placeholder asset; automating the photo choice.

SEQUENCE: after o29.1 (done). Blocks o29.3 - no other product is touched until
this passes.

CURRENT STATUS: ready. o29.1 delivered the product list and confirmed all 15
have usable galleries.
notes:
PROTOCOL AUDIT (added 2026-09-02)

Naming: OK. Goal: acceptance tests are all human :3000 live checks - compliant.
Atomicity note: this issue intentionally spans source+upload+patch+rollback for
ONE product - it is a pipeline-proving spike, SRP = "prove the mechanism". Kept
as one issue because the steps only have value together; footprint capped at 1
product.

RISK ASSESSMENT

== A. OUTCOME RISKS ==
A1. Wrong image sourced - a look-alike different model / variant / colour gets
    published. MITIGATE: human approves the exact photo against the product's
    own spec before publish; source from the manufacturer or official
    distributor page, never image search.
A2. Patch hits the wrong document or field - overwrites a good field or edits a
    sibling product. MITIGATE: target one document by its known id, patch only
    the main-image reference, confirm via read-back query AND the :3000 card
    before "done".
A3. Irreversible CMS damage - prior asset or document state lost. MITIGATE:
    never delete the old asset; rely on Sanity document history; the rollback
    acceptance test must pass before any batch is allowed to start.
A4. Pipeline over-generalises - agent quietly builds and runs a bulk script.
    MITIGATE: OUT OF SCOPE = one product only; footprint = 1 asset + 1 patch.
A5. False "done" - image claimed live without the human's :3000 check.
    MITIGATE: all four acceptance tests are the human's; agent hands off with a
    one-line summary and asserts nothing.
A6. Cache confusion - Next/image or CDN cache makes a changed image look
    unchanged (or a stale one look fixed). MITIGATE: the hard-refresh /
    cache-disabled test; check the served asset id, not just the picture.
A7. Wrong "first product" - ambiguity over which row is #1. MITIGATE: take the
    literal first row of o29.1's ordered artifact.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS ==
Lean path exceptions for this issue, explicit:
B1. ALLOWED: 1 image download from a manufacturer / official source
    (per-download confirmation).
B2. ALLOWED: 1 write to the Sanity production dataset - upload 1 asset, patch 1
    field (per-action confirmation).
B3. ALLOWED: add a Sanity write client / CLI only if absent - check first,
    one-line flag.
B4. NOT allowed: build / tsc / lint / test / dev server / browser automation /
    git / bulk scripting / editing source components.

Expected footprint: 1 new Sanity asset, 1 field patch on 1 document, 1 short
pipeline+rollback note. 0 source files.

REVISED 2026-09-03 (supersedes the scrape-pipeline framing + risk block above).

Fix method is now: promote one of the product's OWN existing gallery photos to
main. No scrape, no download, no rembg, no wrong-product matching. o29.1 verified
all 15 products have full usable galleries.

== A. OUTCOME RISKS (revised) ==
A1. Wrong gallery frame chosen - some galleries lead with a marketing banner
    (Cayin N6iii) or a partial detail crop (Burson Voyager). MITIGATE: human
    picks the frame on a contact sheet; verify on :3000 before "done".
A2. Patch hits wrong doc/field. MITIGATE: patch one document by _id, set only
    the main image reference to an asset already in that doc's gallery; read
    back + check :3000 card.
A3. Not reversible. MITIGATE: do NOT delete the 60x45 placeholder asset; Sanity
    document history is the undo; the rollback acceptance test must pass here.
A4. Scope creep into the other 14 / the out-of-scope buckets. MITIGATE: one
    product only; OUT OF SCOPE list.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS (revised) ==
B1. ALLOWED: one write to Sanity production - set image ref on one document
    (per-action confirmation).
B2. NOT allowed: image download, scrape, running fix-bad-images.ts, deleting
    assets, build / tsc / lint / test / dev server / browser automation for
    verification / git.
Expected footprint: 1 field patch on 1 document. 0 new assets, 0 source files.
close_reason: Pilot done 2026-09-03: Burson Playmate 3 main image promoted from the 60x45 placeholder to gallery image #7, verified on localhost:3000, product page + gallery intact. Mechanism (patch image ref to an existing gallery asset) proven and is reversible via Sanity document history.

title: [Checkout Gates] Flow + cross-cutting questions
description:
SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY

Produce the gating-question cluster for FLOW + CROSS-CUTTING -- the seams, not
the screens -- the sharp, verified, non-leaky yes/no questions later used to
stress-test slice-to-slice transitions and the checkout as a whole, and expose
anything weak, insecure, or amateurish. Parent: sang-logium-vdq. Uses the
rubric + slice map + translation procedure from sang-logium-vdq.1. Sequence: do
this LAST, once clusters 2-6 exist, so it covers only the seams, not the
slices.

THIS ISSUE PRODUCES ONLY QUESTIONS

The deliverable is the question list. Running the questions, finding
vulnerabilities, and fixing them are downstream work, explicitly NOT part of
this issue.

EACH QUESTION MUST BE

- Binary -- yes / no.
- Evidence-named -- states the concrete check that settles it.
- Observable, not implementational (R3) -- about what the customer or store
  owner can see or do; a mechanism concern is reframed via the translation
  procedure or cut.
- Non-leaky -- no honest "yes" while a customer or store owner still has a
  legitimate complaint about the flow as a whole.
- Lean -- deleting it must weaken the "irrefutably professional" conclusion.

GROUNDING FOR THE QUESTION-WRITER (scaffolding -- NOT part of the deliverable;
no term here may appear in a question)

Checkout state lives in one browser cookie that expires after 1 hour and is
size-limited (~4KB, with a soft warning near 3KB); in a real deployment it must
be signed with a proper secret (the code ships a placeholder default). A shared
step indicator runs steps 0-3. A checkout-wide error screen exists. Each step
redirects upstream when a prerequisite is missing (no basket -> basket, no
address -> address step, no shipping -> shipping step). Choosing a new address
clears any shipping already chosen. Language split: address step English,
shipping step Polish, payment / confirmation mostly English. Guest and
authenticated checkout both exist; a guest's orders merge to their account on
later login.

DIMENSIONS THE CLUSTER MUST COVER -- each as an observable outcome

- Security:
  - Can I reach a later checkout step by typing its URL directly, skipping
    address or shipping, and still get to a payment screen? evidence: paste
    the payment-step URL with an empty checkout.
  - Can one person's in-progress checkout ever show another person's basket,
    address, or details? evidence: two browsers / two accounts.
  - When I hand-edit my checkout cookie to change the price or the goods, does
    the next screen ignore the planted data? evidence: the price / items shown
    after the edit -- run this against the deployed site, not only locally.
- Robustness:
  - When my session expires mid-checkout (after address; on the payment page),
    I get a screen that explains it -- not a silent dump to the basket.
  - A large basket that pushes checkout state near its size limit does not
    silently drop items or break a later step.
  - Back and forward across every adjacent step pair keeps my entered data.
  - Refresh on every step keeps me where I was, with my data intact.
  - Two tabs, basket changed in one, never leaves me paying the wrong amount.
  - Abandon checkout and return an hour later -- I get a clear state, not a
    broken half-filled flow.
  - Guard redirects never loop.
  - The step indicator always matches the screen I am actually on.
- Visual polish: the step indicator, header, and layout are consistent across
  all four steps; the checkout error screen is styled like the rest of
  checkout; the English/Polish mix reads as a deliberate bilingual store, not
  as unfinished; typography and spacing are consistent screen to screen at
  every breakpoint.
- UX clarity + trust: I always know which step I am on and how many remain; I
  can go back without losing entered data; the language is consistent enough
  to feel finished; an expired session explains itself rather than dumping
  silently; guest checkout is clearly offered; after signing up, a guest
  order appears in the account.

MUST additionally cover: every adjacent slice-to-slice transition, the whole
happy path end to end, and the major edge paths -- session expiry, abandon-and-
return, decline-then-retry, address change after shipping was chosen.

ACCEPTANCE -- human review of the question list

- A reviewer walking the list against the running checkout cannot name a
  plausible whole-flow customer or store-owner complaint (a broken transition,
  a lost-data back button, an inconsistent or half-translated screen, a silent
  session expiry) that no question would catch.
- No question is vague, non-binary, unfalsifiable, redundant with a per-slice
  question in clusters 2-6, or phrased as a claim about code rather than an
  observable outcome.
- Every question names its evidence.
- The cluster reads in one sitting.

title: [Checkout Gates] Confirmation slice questions
description:
SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY

Produce the gating-question cluster for the CONFIRMATION slice -- the sharp,
verified, non-leaky yes/no questions later used to stress-test it and expose
anything weak, insecure, or amateurish. Parent: sang-logium-vdq. Uses the
rubric + slice map + translation procedure from sang-logium-vdq.1.

THIS ISSUE PRODUCES ONLY QUESTIONS

The deliverable is the question list. Running the questions, finding
vulnerabilities, and fixing them are downstream work, explicitly NOT part of
this issue.

EACH QUESTION MUST BE

- Binary -- yes / no.
- Evidence-named -- states the concrete check that settles it (open a URL, read
  the screen, read the amount off the Stripe / analytics dashboard).
- Observable, not implementational (R3) -- about what the customer or store
  owner can see or do; a mechanism concern is reframed via the translation
  procedure or cut.
- Non-leaky -- no honest "yes" while a customer or store owner still has a
  legitimate complaint about this slice.
- Lean -- deleting it must weaken the "irrefutably professional" conclusion.

GROUNDING FOR THE QUESTION-WRITER (scaffolding -- NOT part of the deliverable;
no term here may appear in a question)

The confirmation screen at /checkout/success. It needs a payment reference in
the URL, else it sends you to the basket. It only shows an order if the current
checkout claims that payment OR an order already exists for it -- otherwise
back to the basket. It re-checks the payment's real status before showing
anything. Outcomes it renders: confirmed (amount, payment-method hint, order
details, a "what happens next" list, continue-shopping / view-orders / support
links), "couldn't verify", payment-provider-down, declined (message + try
again), canceled, processing (refresh button), unexpected. On the confirmed
outcome it also sends a "purchase" event to analytics with the payment id and
amount. Known rough edges to probe: the order lookup on the no-claim path does
not check who is asking; the analytics event can fire again on a hard reload;
the failure outcomes link to /support, which does not exist (/contact does);
the order-receipt area can show a "being prepared" state before the record
lands.

DIMENSIONS THE CLUSTER MUST COVER -- each as an observable outcome

- Security:
  - When I open the confirmation page with someone else's payment reference
    (from a shared link, a forwarded email, a screenshot), am I kept out --
    never shown their name, address, email, or items? evidence: try it in a
    fresh browser / as a different account.
  - Is any card data beyond brand + last four ever shown on the confirmation
    page or present in its page source?
  - Does anything the confirmation page sends to analytics or any third party
    carry my name, email, or address? evidence: browser network panel.
- Robustness:
  - Reloading or reopening the confirmation page keeps showing the same one
    order -- no duplicate, no error, no second charge -- and the store's
    analytics counts the purchase once, not once per reload. evidence:
    analytics dashboard / network panel.
  - Opening the page with a valid reference but no active checkout still shows
    my real order (if it exists) rather than a crash or a wrongful redirect.
  - A payment that was "processing" and then succeeds moves to the confirmed
    screen on refresh, with no dead end.
  - When my order receipt is not ready at first paint, I see a clear "being
    prepared" state with a working refresh -- not a broken card -- and it
    resolves shortly.
  - Every outcome (confirmed, declined, canceled, processing, "couldn't
    verify", provider-down, unexpected) shows its own coherent screen.
  - Pressing Back after a confirmed order shows a sensible screen, not a
    broken payment page and not a re-charge.
- Visual polish: the confirmed screen (success card + order details + "what
  happens next") and every error-outcome screen are clean at 375 / 768 /
  1440; the loading skeleton matches the real card so nothing jumps; icon and
  colour match meaning (confirmed green, hard error red, canceled neutral,
  processing in-progress); no checkout progress stepper shown as if checkout
  were still running.
- UX clarity + trust: "Payment confirmed" and an amount appear ONLY when the
  payment truly went through; the amount shown matches what was charged and
  what the order details say; declined / canceled / processing copy is
  reassuring and tells me exactly what to do; a working way to reach a human
  is present on every failure outcome; "what happens next" promises only what
  the store can actually deliver (no fake tracking, no invented dates);
  "confirmation sent to <email>" appears only when an email was really sent.

Happy path AND every failure outcome AND the transitions in (arriving from
payment) and out (continue shopping / try again / view orders) must each be
represented.

ACCEPTANCE -- human review of the question list

- A reviewer walking the list against the running checkout cannot name a
  plausible customer or store-owner complaint about this slice that no question
  would catch -- including "I was shown a success page but was never charged"
  and "I was charged but shown a failure page".
- No question is vague, non-binary, unfalsifiable, redundant, or phrased as a
  claim about code rather than an observable outcome.
- Every question names its evidence.
- The cluster reads in one sitting.

title: [Checkout Gates] Settlement + order + stock questions
description:
SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY

Produce the gating-question cluster for the SETTLEMENT + ORDER + STOCK slice --
the invisible money path -- the sharp, verified, non-leaky yes/no questions
later used to stress-test it and expose anything weak, insecure, or amateurish.
Parent: sang-logium-vdq. Uses the rubric + slice map + translation procedure
from sang-logium-vdq.1.

THIS ISSUE PRODUCES ONLY QUESTIONS

The deliverable is the question list. Running the questions, finding
vulnerabilities, and fixing them are downstream work, explicitly NOT part of
this issue. This is the highest-risk slice for a store-owner complaint (double
charge, lost order, oversell) -- the questions must be correspondingly sharp.

This slice has almost no customer-facing screen: its observer is the STORE
OWNER, watching the order list in Sanity Studio, product stock, the Stripe
dashboard, and the confirmation email. Every question is phrased as something
the owner (or the customer, at the redirect) can see there.

EACH QUESTION MUST BE

- Binary -- yes / no.
- Evidence-named -- a reproduced double-fire, a replayed notification, a row
  read in the order list, a stock number before/after -- not an assertion.
- Observable, not implementational (R3) -- about what the owner or customer can
  see or do; a mechanism concern is reframed via the translation procedure or
  cut.
- Non-leaky -- no honest "yes" while a customer or store owner still has a
  legitimate complaint.
- Lean -- deleting it must weaken the "irrefutably professional" conclusion.

GROUNDING FOR THE QUESTION-WRITER (scaffolding -- NOT part of the deliverable;
no term here may appear in a question)

Two paths settle a payment and create the order: the return hop when Stripe
sends the customer back (synchronous, treated as non-fatal), and a background
payment notification from Stripe (retried by Stripe on error). Both build the
same order (order number ORD-{year}-{last 6 of the payment id}, items, pricing,
guest vs. account) and both are meant to be idempotent -- if an order already
exists for that payment, skip. A confirmation email is sent (non-fatal). Stock:
per item, check-then-decrement; on insufficient stock it logs and CONTINUES
WITHOUT DECREMENTING ("manual review"); a later check only logs negative stock.
Guest orders are merged to an account on a later login.

DIMENSIONS THE CLUSTER MUST COVER -- each as an observable outcome

- Security (owner-observable):
  - When a hand-made "payment succeeded" notification is sent for a basket
    that was never paid, does the store end up with NO order and NO stock
    change? evidence: order list + product stock in Sanity Studio.
  - When a real payment notification is replayed several times, is there still
    exactly one order and one stock decrement? evidence: order list, stock.
  - Can anyone cause an order to be created for a payment that did not fully
    succeed? evidence: attempt it, check the order list.
  - Does an order record, a log line, or the confirmation email ever contain
    more customer data than the order needs (full card data, anything
    sensitive)? evidence: read an order in Studio, the email, the logs.
- Robustness / correctness:
  - When both settlement paths run at once for the same payment, does the
    store get exactly one order? evidence: order list.
  - Refreshing the post-payment URL does not create a second order or a
    second charge.
  - A payment that is "processing" first and succeeds minutes later still ends
    with exactly one order.
  - When the order store is down at the moment of payment, does the order
    still reliably appear once it recovers -- never zero, never two? evidence:
    order list after recovery.
  - When two orders race for the last unit in stock, is one held back or
    flagged -- the store is never silently oversold, and any oversell is
    owner-visible, not just a buried log.
  - Order numbers do not collide.
  - A failed confirmation email does not lose the order.
- Visual polish: n/a directly -- the only customer-visible output is the
  redirect and its status; confirm every outcome this path can produce is
  actually handled by the confirmation screen (cross-check sang-logium-vdq.6).
- UX clarity + trust: a customer who was charged never ends up back at the
  basket with an error and no order; if something goes wrong, the reference
  shown is enough for support to find the payment; a guest who later signs up
  sees this order in their account.

Happy path AND edge/failure paths AND the transitions in (from the Stripe
redirect) and out (to the confirmation screen) must each be represented.

ACCEPTANCE -- human review of the question list

- A reviewer cannot name a plausible double-charge, lost-order, duplicate-
  order, oversell, or unpaid-order scenario that no question would catch.
- No question is vague, non-binary, unfalsifiable, redundant, or phrased as a
  claim about code rather than an observable outcome.
- Every question names its evidence.
- The cluster reads in one sitting.

title: [Checkout Gates] Shipping slice questions
description:
SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY

Produce the gating-question cluster for the SHIPPING slice -- the sharp,
verified, non-leaky yes/no questions later used to stress-test this slice and
expose anything weak, insecure, or amateurish. Parent: sang-logium-vdq. Uses
the rubric + slice map + translation procedure from sang-logium-vdq.1.

THIS ISSUE PRODUCES ONLY QUESTIONS

The deliverable is the question list. Running the questions, finding
vulnerabilities, and fixing them are downstream work, explicitly NOT part of
this issue.

EACH QUESTION MUST BE

- Binary -- yes / no.
- Evidence-named -- states the concrete check that settles it.
- Observable, not implementational (R3) -- about what the customer or store
  owner can see or do; a mechanism concern is reframed via the translation
  procedure or cut.
- Non-leaky -- no honest "yes" while a customer or store owner still has a
  legitimate complaint about this slice.
- Lean -- deleting it must weaken the "irrefutably professional" conclusion.

GROUNDING FOR THE QUESTION-WRITER (scaffolding -- NOT part of the deliverable;
no term here may appear in a question)

Shipping step. Guards: address + basket present, else redirect upstream. Parcel
sizing derived per basket item; if it cannot be computed -> empty options +
error UI. The real carrier is AlleKurier (PL courier aggregator; PL sender,
delivering to the saved address's postcode) -- NOT Shippo. Options render as a
radio list with Polish copy; inline empty state and inline error banner with a
reload retry. Selecting an option saves { option id, price, method name,
carrier, estimated days }; the price is taken from the client and only checked
to be a positive integer; then redirect to payment.

DIMENSIONS THE CLUSTER MUST COVER -- each as an observable outcome

- Security:
  - When I tamper with the selected shipping option's price before it is saved
    (e.g. down to 0.01 zl), is the amount I am actually charged still the real
    carrier price for that option? evidence: Stripe dashboard amount for the
    payment.
  - When I try to pay against a shipping option that was never offered to me,
    or an older cheaper quote from an earlier visit, is it rejected? evidence:
    the payment total / an error on the shipping step.
- Robustness:
  - When the carrier service is down, slow, returns nothing, or returns a
    partial list, the shipping page shows a clear message and a working retry
    -- no infinite spinner, no stack trace, no empty page.
  - When parcel sizing cannot be worked out for a basket, I get a clear state,
    not a crash.
  - When I changed my address upstream, the options shown are for the new
    address, not stale ones.
  - A very large or heavy basket still produces sane options or a clear
    "contact us" message.
  - The price shown on an option equals the amount added to my total to the
    cent; a missing delivery estimate degrades gracefully ("estimate
    unavailable", never "undefined").
- Visual polish: the option list, its selected state, the empty state and the
  error banner are clean at 375 / 768 / 1440; the mobile CTA is reachable;
  prices align and do not truncate.
- UX clarity + trust: the shipping page being in Polish while the address page
  was in English -- does it read as a deliberate bilingual store or a jarring
  half-translation; delivery estimates are attributed to a carrier and read as
  honest; I can tell carrier apart from service level; the price I see here is
  exactly the price I pay later.

Happy path AND edge/failure paths AND the transitions in (from address) and out
(to payment) must each be represented.

ACCEPTANCE -- human review of the question list

- A reviewer walking the list against the running checkout cannot name a
  plausible customer or store-owner complaint about this slice that no question
  would catch.
- No question is vague, non-binary, unfalsifiable, redundant, or phrased as a
  claim about code rather than an observable outcome.
- Every question names its evidence.
- The cluster reads in one sitting.

description:

Produce the gating-question cluster for the ENTRY + ADDRESS slice -- the sharp,
verified, non-leaky yes/no questions later used to stress-test this slice and
expose anything weak, insecure, or amateurish. Parent: sang-logium-vdq. Uses

THIS ISSUE PRODUCES ONLY QUESTIONS

The deliverable is the question list. Running the questions, finding
vulnerabilities, and fixing them are downstream work, explicitly NOT part of
this issue.

EACH QUESTION MUST BE

- Binary -- yes / no, no "sort of".
- Evidence-named -- states the concrete check that settles it: a live action on
  localhost:3000, a reproduced attempt that visibly fails, a side-by-side
  visual comparison, a figure read off the Stripe dashboard, a row in the
  order list.
- Observable, not implementational (R3) -- about what the customer or store
  owner can see or do; never names a file, endpoint, config value, or internal
  mechanism. A mechanism concern is reframed via the translation procedure or
  cut.
- Non-leaky -- no honest "yes" while a customer or store owner still has a
  legitimate complaint about this slice.
- Lean -- if deleting it does not weaken the "irrefutably professional"
  conclusion, delete it.

GROUNDING FOR THE QUESTION-WRITER (scaffolding -- NOT part of the deliverable;
no term here may appear in a question)

Basket "Checkout" button starts checkout with { productId, quantity } only (no
price, no stock carried from the client) -> address screen. Address form
(English UI): first/last name, phone, country (PL only), city, street, street
number, postal code. Submit -> Google Address Validation -> ACCEPT / FIX /
CONFIRM. Non-ACCEPT: inline error plus a "Continue with entered address" escape
hatch that resubmits skipping validation. ACCEPT: address saved, any previously
chosen shipping is invalidated, redirect to the shipping step. Guard: empty /
all-out-of-stock basket -> /basket.

DIMENSIONS THE CLUSTER MUST COVER -- each as an observable outcome

- Security:
  - When I alter what the "Checkout" button sends (extra fields, a planted
    price or stock number, a negative or huge quantity, a duplicated line), do
    the price I am eventually asked to pay and the quantities in my order still
    match only what was really in my basket? evidence: payment-page total and
    the final order row.
  - When I put markup or a script snippet into an address field, does it show
    as plain text everywhere it is later displayed -- order confirmation, order
    list, confirmation email -- with nothing executing? evidence: view each
    surface.
  - When I use the escape hatch with obviously bad address data, does the rest
    of checkout still behave sanely (no later crash, the bad address visible
    for me to correct) rather than silently carrying junk toward payment?
    evidence: complete the flow, inspect the payment screen and the order.
- Robustness:
  - When I double-click "Checkout" or click it on a slow connection, do I land
    on exactly one address screen -- no duplicate start, no stuck spinner?
  - When I press Back from shipping, is my address form still filled with what
    I typed, including un-saved edits -- not blanked or reverted?
  - When address validation says "fix this" vs "confirm this", do I get a
    clear, different message for each, and can I always proceed?
  - When the address-validation service is slow or down, can I still complete
    the address step with a clear explanation, rather than being blocked with
    no way forward?
  - Empty or whitespace-only required fields, and a malformed Polish postal
    code, are each rejected at the form with a specific message.
  - When I change my address after a shipping option was chosen, is the old
    shipping choice and price cleared so I cannot pay against a stale rate?
    evidence: the shipping and payment screens after the edit.
- Visual polish: the address form, its error state and its loading state are
  clean and unbroken at 375 / 768 / 1440; the escape-hatch button is visibly
  secondary to the primary submit; the step indicator shows the correct step.
- UX clarity + trust: it is obvious why an address was rejected and what to do
  next; the escape hatch reads as a safe fallback, not "give up"; "Poland only"
  is clear before I fill the whole form; the reason a phone number is required
  is stated.

Happy path AND edge/failure paths AND the transitions into this slice (from the
basket) and out of it (to shipping) must each be represented.

ACCEPTANCE -- human review of the question list

- A reviewer walking the list against the running checkout cannot name a

- No question is vague, non-binary, unfalsifiable, redundant, or phrased as a

title: [Checkout Gates] Question rubric + slice map
description:
SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY

Define the instrument before it is built: what makes a checkout gating question
a real gate rather than a leaky or code-level one, and lock the slice
boundaries that children 2-7 will fill in. Parent: sang-logium-vdq.

THIS ISSUE PRODUCES

1. The question rubric -- the test every gating question in every sibling must
   pass:

   - R1 Binary: answerable yes / no. No scale, no "mostly", no "depends".
   - R2 Evidence-named: the question itself states how a person settles it --
     a live action on localhost:3000, a reproduced attempt that visibly fails,
     a side-by-side visual comparison, a figure read off the Stripe / analytics
     dashboard, a row read in the store's order list, the confirmation email.
   - R3 Observable, not implementational: the question asks about something a
     customer or the store owner can SEE or DO. It must not name -- or turn on
     the existence or wording of -- a file, function, route, endpoint, config
     value, secret, header, cookie flag, database, or internal mechanism.
     Banned unless the customer sees the word on screen: "server-side",
     "validated", "webhook", "signature", "endpoint", "session cookie",
     "iron-session", "idempotent / idempotency", "Sanity", "metadata", "API
     key", "route handler", "fallback", "hook". A candidate that names a
     mechanism is REWRITTEN via the translation procedure (point 2) or cut.
   - R4 Non-leaky: no honest "yes" can coexist with a legitimate customer or
     store-owner complaint about that slice.
   - R5 Lean: deleting the question must weaken the "irrefutably professional"
     conclusion, or it is cut.
   - R6 Policy-neutral: it must not presume a business rule (a price, a
     quantity cap, a required field) the owner has not stated; where the real
     concern is an undefined policy, ask whether that policy is intentional,
     consistent and disclosed -- never whether one value is enforced.

   Each question carries >=1 dimension tag: security / robustness / visual /
   trust -- where "security" means an observable bad outcome (money lost,
   another person's data seen, an order that should not stand), not a code
   audit item.

2. The translation procedure -- how a real concern about a mechanism becomes a
   valid question:
   a. Name what the mechanism exists to guarantee for a person.
   b. Describe the action that breaks that guarantee if the mechanism is
      absent or wrong -- as something a customer or outsider actually does.
   c. State the observable result that proves pass/fail, and where a person
      sees it.
   d. If no such observable result exists, the concern is not a gating
      question for this epic -- drop it; it belongs to a code review.
   Worked: "is the webhook signature verified" -> guarantee: only real Stripe
   payments create orders -> action: send a hand-made payment-succeeded
   notification for a basket that was never paid -> observable: a paid order
   appears in the order list / stock drops -> question: "When a forged payment
   notification is sent for a basket I never paid for, does the store still
   end up with no order and no stock change? -- evidence: order list + product
   stock in Sanity Studio".

3. The leanness test -- a concrete procedure for deciding a question is fat and
   should be cut or merged. Includes a TRANSLATION check: if the question only
   makes sense to someone reading the code, it fails R3 -- rewrite or cut.

4. The slice map -- the final list of checkout slices plus the whole-system
   slice, each with a one-line boundary statement, so no checkout behaviour is
   homeless and no two clusters overlap. Boundaries are drawn in terms of what
   the customer is doing (which screen, which transition), grounded against the
   real source (app/checkout/**, app/actions/checkout/**, app/api/checkout/**,
   app/api/webhooks/stripe/**, lib/checkout/**, lib/session.ts) -- NOT from
   _project/ or docs/ notes, which are stale (they still describe Shippo and an
   atomic reservation document; neither exists). The source is how the writer
   knows what to probe; it must not surface in the questions.

5. A worked example: 2-3 model gating questions and 3-4 rejected ones -- at
   least two rejected specifically for being code-level rather than observable,
   each then shown reframed by the translation procedure.

NOT THIS ISSUE

Writing the per-slice clusters (children 2-7). No checkout code is audited for
defects and nothing is fixed.

ACCEPTANCE -- human review

- Given the rubric, two people classify the same candidate question the same
  way (valid vs leaky vs code-level) in the large majority of cases.
- The slice map covers every route, handler and lib file in the checkout
  system; a reviewer cannot name a checkout behaviour that falls in no slice.
- The worked example's rejects are recognisably the kind of vague, amateurish,
  or code-level question that must never leak through -- and each is shown
  successfully reframed as an observable outcome.

draft predates them and must be re-checked against them. Blocks 2-7.

title: EPIC Checkout Gating Questions
description:
GOAL

Produce the complete, leanest-possible set of professional GATING QUESTIONS for
the checkout system -- one cluster per checkout slice, plus one whole-system
cluster (slice-to-slice transitions and cross-cutting concerns) -- and verify
each question is legitimate: sharp enough to use directly as a stress test that
exposes real defects, and collectively strong enough that "every question
answers yes" forces the conclusion "this checkout is professional -- nothing
amateurish, no leak a customer or the (hypothetical) store owner could
legitimately complain about".

WHAT KIND OF QUESTION THIS EPIC PRODUCES -- AND WHAT IT DOES NOT

Every gating question is an OBSERVABLE OUTCOME that a customer or the store
owner can check by USING the running site (localhost:3000), reading a rendered
screen, or looking at the store's own records -- the Stripe dashboard, the
order list in Sanity Studio, the analytics dashboard, the confirmation email.

A gating question is NEVER a question about the code: not about a file,
function, route, endpoint, config value, secret, header, cookie flag, database,
or internal mechanism. "Is the webhook signature verified", "is the rate id
validated server-side", "does the order lookup check ownership", "is the
session cookie httpOnly" are all DISQUALIFIED as written. The concern behind
each is real -- but it must be expressed as the observable thing that goes
wrong for a person when the mechanism fails, plus the evidence that settles it.
Example: not "is the webhook signature verified" but "when a forged payment
notification is sent for a basket I never paid for, does the store still end up
with no order and no stock change? -- evidence: order list + product stock in
Sanity Studio".

sang-logium-vdq.1 makes this rule precise (rubric test R3) and gives the
translation procedure that turns a mechanism concern into a valid question.
Every sibling cluster obeys it.

SCOPE OF THIS EPIC IS THE QUESTIONS ONLY. Running the stress tests, finding
vulnerabilities, and fixing them are downstream work -- separate epics. This
epic delivers the instrument and proves the instrument is trustworthy.

Every gating question must be:

- Binary -- yes / no, no scale, no "sort of".
- Evidence-named -- the question states how a person settles it: a live action
  on localhost:3000, a screen compared side by side, a figure read off the
  Stripe / analytics dashboard, a row read in the store's order list.
- Observable, not implementational -- see the rule above and R3 in vdq.1.
- Non-leaky -- no honest "yes" can coexist with a legitimate customer or
  store-owner complaint about that slice.
- Lean -- zero fat; if deleting it does not weaken the "irrefutably
  professional" conclusion, it is deleted.

Dimensions every slice cluster covers for its portion of the flow -- each
stated as what a person experiences:

- Security -- expressed as "can a customer or an outsider make the store lose
  money, see another person's data, or place an order that should not stand" --
  never as a code-level check.
- Robustness / correctness -- every state a customer can land in (loading,
  empty, error, timeout, partial, retried) shows a coherent screen; no order
  is lost or duplicated; stock never silently drifts.
- Visual polish -- professional at every supported breakpoint (375 / 768 /
  1440), design-system aligned, no layout breakage.
- UX clarity and trust -- at every moment the customer understands what is
  happening, what to do next, and what went wrong; nothing on the page invites
  distrust.

ACCEPTANCE -- human review of the deliverable:

- Every checkout slice has a cluster, and the whole-system cluster exists and
  covers transitions plus cross-cutting concerns (re-entry, refresh, back
  button, abandonment, session expiry, guest vs. authenticated).
- Walking the combined list against the running checkout, a reviewer cannot
  name a plausible customer or store-owner complaint that no question catches.
- A reviewer cannot point to any question that is vague, non-binary,
  unfalsifiable, redundant, OR phrased as a claim about code rather than an
  observable outcome.
- Each question names the concrete evidence that would settle it yes or no.
- The full list is small enough to read in one sitting.

slice map and blocks the rest.

title: EPIC Brand Data Integrity
description:
ACCEPTANCE TESTS

- When I open the Brand filter on /products/headphones and /products, then every maker appears exactly once, with no name repeated anywhere in the list.
- When I look for any maker that has products in the catalogue, then it appears as a selectable row in the Brand filter (no maker with products is missing).
- When I tick any brand, then the results include every product from that maker, and the count shown next to the brand equals the number of results.
- When I scan the Brand list, then no internal test or placeholder entries appear.
- When I open a product detail page, then its brand label and brand link still resolve correctly (no broken or missing brand).

CURRENT STATUS: not started. Data-only epic - no changes to filter, query, or UI code. Supersedes the data half of the now-closed sang-logium-agq.3. Root cause and full dataset audit in NOTES.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE

The brand filter code (sanity-cms/lib/products/getBrandFacets.ts) is correct - it emits
one row per `brand` document that has a slug and >= 1 product. The rows are wrong because
the `brand` documents are wrong. This is a CMS data-integrity problem, not a code bug.

DATASET AUDIT (2026-09-02, read-only GROQ against production - 143 brand docs)

1. Duplicate documents for one maker (products split across both):
   Meze: "meze"(15) + "meze-audio"(26)          -> canonical "meze", target 41
   Kanto: "kanto"(24) + "kanto-living"(3)        -> human ruling needed (sub-brand?)
   HiFiMan: "HiFiMan" no-slug (9) + "hifiman"(18) -> canonical "hifiman", target 27
   Chord: "Chord" no-slug (3) + "chord-electronics"(8) -> target 11
   iFi: "iFi" no-slug (11) + "ifi-audio"(36)     -> target 47
   Burson: "Burson" no-slug (1) + "burson-audio"(15) -> target 16
   Ferrum: "Ferrum" no-slug (1) + "ferrum-audio"(3)  -> target 4
   Sony: "sony"(21) + "sony-mobile"(0)           -> human ruling needed (likely keep separate)

2. Missing slug: 47 brand docs have >0 products but no slug.current, so they never appear
   as a filter row. 206 products are unfilterable by brand. 5 of the 47 are the slugless
   twins above (handled by merge, not slug-add). ~42 are standalone (Cambridge Audio 3,
   Astell&Kern 20, Campfire Audio 5, Cayin 12, Wicked Cushions 24, XDuoo 11, Spinfit 10,
   ddHiFi 10, Eletech 9, Yulong 7, Sensaphonics 7, Gustard 6, and ~30 more).

3. Test / placeholder docs in production: "Test Brand" x4, "Test Brand Alpha",
   "Test Brand Beta", "The Last Factory" - all count 0. (Kicker, Mountson, Ortofon,
   Panamax also count 0 but are real brands - leave them.)

END STATE: ~127 brand docs, one per real maker, each with a unique slug; every product
brand-> ref points at its canonical doc; no placeholder docs. Zero app source changes.

== A. OUTCOME RISKS ==
A1. Merging genuinely distinct brands (Sony/Sony Mobile, Kanto/Kanto Living).
    MITIGATE: merge map is human-approved in child 1 before any write; when in doubt, keep
    as two.
A2. Losing / mis-pointing products; deleting a doc that still has inbound refs.
    MITIGATE: full export snapshot before any write; Sanity blocks deletion while strong
    refs exist - use that as the gate; delete only after loser inbound-ref count is 0 AND
    winner count == pre-merge sum.
A3. Slug collision or off-convention slug; breaks a hardcoded reference.
    MITIGATE: check slug uniqueness across all 143 docs before writing; grep repo for
    hardcoded brand slugs; follow the existing lowercase-hyphen pattern verbatim.
A4. Scope creep into filter / query / UI code.
    MITIGATE: epic is data-only. Any code guard (e.g. surface slugless brands) is a
    separate issue outside this epic with its own decision.
A5. Other brand-data consumers break (brand pages, sitemap, build-time catalogue VFS
    index, homepage brand refs, Studio).
    MITIGATE: child 1 lists every code path reading brand slug/id; re-point by _id so refs
    survive; regenerate the catalogue index after child 3 (human runs it).
A6. Collision with in-progress sang-logium-3a9 (brand filter checkbox + URL).
    MITIGATE: serialize - no brand data migration while 3a9 touches brand filter code.
A7. Partial completion leaves the filter worse (slugging a twin before merging it).
    MITIGATE: sequencing - twins are merged in child 3, never slugged in child 2; each
    child leaves the filter coherent.
A8. False "done" without the live check.
    MITIGATE: re-run the read-only inventory query as before/after evidence; hand each
    child's localhost:3000 spot-check to the human.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS ==
This epic is production data mutation - it CANNOT be "edit source only, hand to :3000".
Explicit exceptions:
B1. Writes to production Sanity are the deliverable. Guardrail: export/snapshot first;
    small batches; verify after each; one maker at a time for merges.
B2. A migration script is permitted and preferred over dozens of manual Studio edits, but
    must dry-run first and print every mutation, require an explicit go, batch, and verify.
    No silent bulk writes. @sanity/client already installed; needs a write token from .env.
B3. Still NO: next build, tsc / ts-check, project lint, test runs, agent-run dev server,
    browser automation for verification, npm install, agent git commit/push.
B4. The read-only inventory query is required (before/after evidence), not just allowed.
B5. No subagents. One reference doc (the inventory/plan), not a sprawl of audit files.
B6. After child 3, scripts/build-catalogue-index.mjs may need a re-run if it caches brand
    data - flag it, human runs it.

Expected footprint: 1 new reference doc, 1 optional migration script (scripts/temp-* or
scratch), ~42 slug adds + ~9 merges + ~7 deletes as Sanity mutations. 0 app source
changes, 0 dependencies.

SEQUENCE: child 1 (plan, human-approved) -> child 2 (slug adds, additive) -> child 3
(merges + test-doc deletes, one maker at a time).

STATUS 2026-09-03: 2 of 3 children done.
- g8q.1 CLOSED — deliverable _project/reports/brand-data-integrity-inventory.md
  (inventory + MERGE/SLUG/DELETE maps + consumer list).
- All 6 OPEN RULINGS resolved by Munrhalls 2026-09-02. Supersedes the two
  "human ruling needed" lines in the DATASET AUDIT above: Kanto + Kanto Living
  = MERGE (target 27); Sony Mobile = DELETE (0 products), NOT a merge with Sony.
- g8q.2 CLOSED — 42 standalone slugs written to production 2026-09-03. Verified

  merge-losers only). No collisions.
- g8q.3 OPEN, not started — 7 merges + 8 deletes + Hifiman->HiFiMan rename +

Epic acceptance tests remain unverified end-to-end because the brand facet UI is
currently removed pending rebuild — correctness evidence to date is GROQ
before/after, not a localhost:3000 filter check.

STATUS 2026-09-03: all 3 children CLOSED.
- g8q.1 — plan/inventory deliverable.
- g8q.2 — 42 standalone slugs written to production.
- g8q.3 — 7 merges + 8 deletes + Hifiman->HiFiMan rename + 4 /brand redirects. EXECUTED 2026-09-03.
END STATE reached: brand docs 143 -> 128, every doc has a unique slug (slugless 0, duplicate slug strings 0), 0 dangling product->brand refs, 1035 products unchanged. Deliverable §9 has the full execution record.
REMAINING: epic acceptance tests (the Brand filter on /products) cannot be live-checked yet — the brand facet UI is removed pending rebuild. The data layer is now correct; verify the epic ATs when that UI ships. Consider closing this epic as data-complete and tracking the UI rebuild separately.

UPDATE 2026-09-03: g8q.3 live-checked by human on localhost:3000 — acceptance tests 1-4 PASS (no duplicate rows, merged-brand results+counts correct, no placeholder rows, PDP brand label/link resolve). The brand facet UI is present after all. These overlap the epic ATs directly. Epic data work is complete and verified; remaining epic-level gap is only whether the g8q.2 newly-slugged makers (Cambridge Audio, Astell&Kern, etc.) have been eyeballed in the filter. Ready to close pending that spot-check.

title: Product Grid: mobile card hierarchy, sizing, quiet wishlist
description:
GOAL

On mobile (320-430px), the product-listing grid -- the grid rhythm, the card,
and the card internals -- reads as a calm, professional e-commerce listing:
balanced proportions, clear visual hierarchy (image supports, title anchors,
price second, add + wishlist quiet), even gutters, and product titles that are
mostly readable rather than every one truncated. Fully aligned to
tailwind.config.ts tokens. Target 8+/10 on mobile card layout / hierarchy /
sizing, human live-check on :3000.

Standalone. Depends on `sang-logium-6cm` -- [Product Cards] Shared design
tokens (the brand/title/price/add type scale must be set first). Coordinates
with `sang-logium-dbu` -- [Filters] Product grid sizing fits device space,
which owns ProductCard.tsx desktop / row composition: THIS issue changes only
the mobile (< sm / 640px) rendering plus WishlistButton.tsx, and lands AFTER
dbu if dbu is mid-flight, to avoid diff conflicts.

WHAT'S WRONG NOW (observed at 320px on /products/headphones, 2-up grid)

- WishlistButton (`h-10 w-10` rounded-full, `border-border-primary` +
  `bg-surface-elevated` fill, Heart `h-5 w-5`, `right-3 top-3`, z-20): a loud
  ~40px high-contrast chip on a ~130px card. It competes with the product
  image and rivals the gold Add button. A listing-card favourite must be a
  quiet tertiary mark tucked into the corner. (design-system.md:91 already
  flags this `rounded-full` badge as off-system.)
- Every product title truncates at 2 lines ("HarmonicDyne x Z Reviews Er...",
  "Sennheiser HD 560S Open-..."). Causes: (a) the brand is shown as an eyebrow
  AND repeated at the start of the title, (b) title size vs the ~106px content
  width, (c) the 24px `gap-6` gutter stealing width from a 132px card.
- `min-h-[2.5em]` on the title (ProductCard.tsx:49) is an arbitrary bracket
  value -- off the design system.
- Grid gutter `gap-6` (24px, from gridLayout.ts `productGridClass`) is ~18% of
  a 132px card -- disproportionate for mobile; one fixed gutter is applied at
  every width.
- Hierarchy is dissonant: the bright `bg-surface-productImage` block, the loud
  wishlist chip, and the gold `btn-product-add` all shout, while the brand and
  title -- the actual identifying content -- are the weakest elements.
- Card padding: `card-product-dark` (24px) is overridden with `!p-0` then
  re-applied ad-hoc as `p-3` / `px-3 pb-3` -- no single internal rhythm.

DESIGN

- Wishlist: on the listing card, drop the filled background + border; render
  the heart as a plain icon (no chrome, or at most a subtle scrim for
  contrast), smaller visual mark, tighter into the true top-right corner.
  Keep a >= 44px hit area via padding while the visible mark stays small
  (small-visual / large-invisible-hit-slop). Keep aria-label / title / the
  signed-out redirect unchanged. NOTE: WishlistButton hardcodes its chrome in
  a raw template string (no cn / tailwind-merge), so a plain `className`
  override will not reliably win -- add a `variant` (or `size`) prop, default
  = today's PDP appearance, and select the quiet variant from ProductCard.
  ProductInfo.tsx (PDP, the only other call site) must render identically to
  now.
- Title: keep `line-clamp-2` as a safety net, but strip a leading brand token
  from the VISIBLE title when it exactly (case-insensitive) matches
  `product.brand.name` and the brand eyebrow is shown; full name stays in the
  image `alt` and the link `aria-label`. Replace `min-h-[2.5em]` with the
  spacing token equal to two title lines at the 6cm line-height; flag if no
  token fits.
- Grid gutter: make the mobile gutter proportional to the card -- a smaller
  spacing-scale step at base, restored to `gap-6` at `sm:` (mobile-first
  additive, matching gridLayout.ts's own base-then-`sm:` pattern). One edit in
  gridLayout.ts; applies to every product grid (category, all-products,
  search, wishlist).
- Internal padding: one consistent spacing-scale value on all sides of the
  content / price block; keep the image flush (`!p-0` + edge-to-edge figure)
  as dbu established.
- Hierarchy: title is the anchor (readable, not undersized), price second,
  Add tertiary-but-tappable, wishlist quietest -- achieved through the 6cm
  token sizes + the wishlist de-emphasis. Do NOT restyle the image block.
- Any h- / min-h- / max-h- / aspect- change gets the CLAUDE.md mandatory
  height-sizing diff review.

OUT OF SCOPE

- Token VALUES in tailwind.config.ts (`sang-logium-6cm`) -- flag a missing
  step, do not add one here.
- ProductCard.tsx desktop / >= sm composition, the two grid skeletons, the
  `label` prop (`sang-logium-dbu`).
- The grid COLUMN mechanism (`grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-products`,
  `gridTemplateColumns.products`) -- done, leave it.
- Image aspect ratio, `bg-surface-productImage` colour, `mix-blend-multiply`.
- BasketControls.tsx internals, the filter / sort surface, data / GROQ.
- Homepage card variants -- IemCard / AccessoryCard (`sang-logium-5g4.1`),
  DacCard / Featured (`sang-logium-69m`).

ACCEPTANCE -- human live-check on :3000 at 320 / 375 / 430, plus 1024+ for
no-regression, on /products/headphones AND one search results page:

1. The wishlist heart is a small quiet mark in the top-right corner -- no
   filled chip, does not compete with the image or the Add button -- and its
   tap area is still >= 44px; tapping it does not navigate to the PDP. The PDP
   wishlist button is unchanged.
2. Most product titles are readable without truncation; a long title clamps to
   2 lines with ellipsis; the brand is not repeated between the eyebrow and
   the visible title.
3. In a 2-up row with mixed title lengths, every card is the same height,
   price and Add sit on a shared baseline at the card bottom, and internal
   padding looks even on all sides.
4. The gutter between mobile cards looks proportional (not a wide channel);
   no horizontal scroll at any width; the >= sm grid and card are visually
   unchanged from before.

- Diff is tailwind.config.ts tokens only (or an explicit flag for a missing
  token). No new arbitrary bracket values.

CURRENT STATUS: Not started. Depends on `sang-logium-6cm` (token scale);
coordinate with in-progress `sang-logium-dbu` (shares ProductCard.tsx --
mobile-only edits here, land after dbu).
notes:
RISK ASSESSMENT (added 2026-08-31)

EXECUTOR: Claude Sonnet, high effort. Rationale: three files, a shared layout
primitive (gridLayout.ts feeds 4+ grids), the "WishlistButton must not change
on the PDP" constraint (needs a prop, not a className override, because the
button has no cn/tailwind-merge), the min-h token math, and the CLAUDE.md
height-sizing review gate. Not a cheap-model job.

== A. OUTCOME RISKS ==
A1. Collision with in-progress dbu on ProductCard.tsx. MITIGATE: mobile-only
    classNames (base value, restore at `sm:`); touch no `sm:`+ class dbu owns;
    land after dbu.
A2. WishlistButton change leaks to the PDP (ProductInfo.tsx) or anywhere else.
    MITIGATE: only 2 call sites -- ProductCard (listing) and ProductInfo (PDP).
    Add a `variant`/`size` prop; DEFAULT keeps today's exact classes so the PDP
    renders identically; ProductCard opts into the quiet variant. Do not
    rewrite the button's base string.
A3. Off-design-system values -- arbitrary gap / padding / size / min-h instead
    of spacing / fontSize tokens. MITIGATE: read tailwind.config.ts; tokens
    only; `min-h-[2.5em]` is itself the bug -- replace with a token, do not add
    more brackets. Flag a missing step to 6cm.
A4. gridLayout.ts gutter edit regresses desktop or the other grids (search,
    wishlist, all-products). MITIGATE: base value + `sm:gap-6` restore; human
    checks a search page too, not just category.
A5. `xs:` cascade trap -- `xs` (475px) is emitted AFTER `sm/md/lg` in this
    repo, so an `xs:` class wins at every desktop width (gridLayout.ts
    comment). MITIGATE: never use `xs:` for a value that must also hold at
    desktop; base + `sm:` only.
A6. Height-sizing ownership bug on the title min-h or any figure height.
    MITIGATE: run the CLAUDE.md mandatory height-sizing diff review on every
    h- / min-h- / max-h- / aspect- change.
A7. Scope creep into the image block, the column mechanism, dbu's composition,
    or 6cm's token values. MITIGATE: restate OUT OF SCOPE before starting; stop
    and flag if a fix needs any of them.
A8. Brand-token stripping mangles a title that legitimately starts with a word
    resembling the brand. MITIGATE: strip only an exact case-insensitive match
    of `product.brand.name` as the leading token, only when the eyebrow is
    shown; full name stays in alt / aria.
A9. False "verified" -- "quiet", "balanced", "readable hierarchy" are the
    human's call on :3000. MITIGATE: state what changed and which token drove
    it; hand the 8+/10 verdict to the human.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS ==
Lean path = edit ProductCard.tsx + WishlistButton.tsx (add a variant prop) +
gridLayout.ts only, hand off to the human on :3000.
B1. No build / tsc / ts-check / lint.
B2. No test runs, no writing tests.
B3. No agent-run dev server, no browser automation / device emulation.
B4. No npm install / new dependency.
B5. No git -- no branch, commit, push.
B6. No subagents; read the three files + tailwind.config.ts + gridLayout.ts +
    ProductInfo.tsx inline. No new docs.
B7. Minimal diff -- no reformatting untouched lines; do not "tidy" dbu's or
    6cm's in-flight changes.

Expected footprint: className edits in
app/components/features/products/ProductCard.tsx and
app/components/features/products/gridLayout.ts; a `variant`/`size` prop added
to app/components/features/wishlist/WishlistButton.tsx (default unchanged). No
new files. No deps / config / tooling changes. Any token gap is flagged to
`sang-logium-6cm`, not filled here.

title: [Cards] Brand eyebrow above title, out of image area
description:
GOAL

On every homepage IEM card and Accessory card, at every breakpoint, the brand
name renders once as an eyebrow/overline directly above the product title
(Amazon style) -- never inside or overlapping the product image.

Child of `sang-logium-5g4` -- EPIC Card Harmony. Blocks
`sang-logium-5g4.1` -- [Cards] IEM + Accessory card internals -> design system
(mechanical relocation lands first, then .1 tunes the rest). Owns the brand
line only, in IemCard.tsx and AccessoryCard.tsx.

WHAT'S WRONG NOW
- Brand is rendered twice per card: an absolutely-positioned span inside the
  image area (hidden md:block) and a second span below the image (md:hidden).
- On mobile the brand overlaps the product image / the promo badge (see
  screenshots: "64 AUDIO" behind "NEW ARRIVAL", "SVS" / "AUDIOQUEST" over the
  cable photos).

DESIGN
- Delete both existing brand spans.
- Render one brand line directly above the <h3> product title, using
  type-product-brand from tailwind.config.ts (10px, uppercase, tracked,
  caption color) -- an eyebrow, not bold body text.
- The image area contains only the image and the promo badge (NEW ARRIVAL /
  etc.) -- no text.
- IemCard keeps its brandName-derivation fallback (brand?.name, else first
  words of the product name); AccessoryCard renders the line only when
  item.brand?.name exists.
- The two files render the brand block identically.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Title weight / clamp / card height / button size -- all sang-logium-5g4.1.
- The promo badge position/style; the image ratio; padding.
- DacCard, ProductCard, data/query changes.
- Editing any tailwind.config.ts token.

ACCEPTANCE -- human live-check on :3000 at 375 / 768 / 1024-short / 1440
(max 4 tests):
1. Every card shows the brand exactly once, on its own line directly above the
   product title, at all four widths.
2. No text sits inside or over the product image -- only the promo badge.
3. The brand line is the type-product-brand eyebrow style (small, uppercase,
   letter-spaced, caption color), not bold.
4. IemCard and AccessoryCard render the brand block identically; no horizontal
   overflow at any width.

CURRENT STATUS: Not started.
notes:

EXECUTOR: Claude Sonnet, low effort. Rationale: mechanical DOM move + one
existing token (type-product-brand) used verbatim; near-zero hallucination
surface. Human confirms overlap is gone on :3000.

    in the image. MITIGATE: grep each file for the brand after editing; exactly
    one brand render, above the title.
A2. Re-inventing a brand style instead of type-product-brand. MITIGATE: use the
    token class verbatim; if it needs a tweak, flag it, don't inline values.
A3. Dropping IemCard's brandName fallback (brand?.name || first words of name).
    MITIGATE: keep the fallback; only AccessoryCard is conditional on
    item.brand?.name.
A4. Divergence between the two files. MITIGATE: diff IemCard vs AccessoryCard;
    brand block identical.
A5. Collision with sang-logium-5g4.1 (same two files). MITIGATE: this lands
    first (blocks .1); .1 rebases on the result.
A6. False "verified" -- only the human's :3000 check confirms the overlap is
    gone at each width. MITIGATE: hand off the verdict.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS ==
Lean path = edit the brand markup in IemCard.tsx + AccessoryCard.tsx, hand off.
B1. No build / tsc / ts-check / lint.
B2. No test runs, no writing tests.
B3. No agent-run dev server, no browser automation / device emulation.
B4. No npm install.
B5. No git.
