- When the fix issues are later created, then this backlog is the single source they are cut from.

DELIVERABLE: exactly one file at _project/audits/intel-consolidation-backlog.md — severity-ranked (P0/P1/P2) list, each finding with evidence (file:line or live URL + observed behaviour), the user-visible impact, and a one-line fix direction. No code changes.

CURRENT STATUS: not started.
notes:
RISK ASSESSMENT (added 2026-09-02)

NOTE ON PROTOCOL FIT: this is a read-only intelligence task, not an implementation task.
Goal is acceptance tests on the DELIVERABLE (the findings doc), not on localhost:3000.
Runs safely in parallel with sibling audits because it edits no source and writes one
uniquely-named file.

== A. OUTCOME RISKS ==
A1. Scope creep - the audit starts fixing things. MITIGATE: findings only; zero source edits; every gap becomes a separate fix issue later, not now.
A2. Overlap with a sibling audit (same gap logged twice). MITIGATE: stay strictly inside this issue's layer; cross-layer gaps get a one-line "see <other layer>" pointer, not a full writeup.
A3. Hallucinated findings - plausible-sounding issues that are not real at runtime. MITIGATE: every finding cites a file:line or a live URL + what was observed; no finding without evidence.
A4. Severity inflation - everything marked P0. MITIGATE: P0 = a professional evaluator would visibly wince; P1 = they would note it; P2 = polish. Most findings are P1/P2.
A5. Stale-doc-as-authority - trusting an old _project audit over current code. MITIGATE: verify against current HEAD; cite the file you actually read.
A6. False "looks fine" pass on something only a live check catches. MITIGATE: state what was checked statically vs. on the live site; flag anything needing the human's :3000 check.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS ==
Lean path = READ source + inspect the live production site (https://sanglogium.com) as text/DOM/computed-style. Write exactly ONE findings doc. Nothing else.
B1. No source edits, no fixes, no refactors.
B2. No build / tsc / lint / test / dev server.
B3. Live inspection is against DEPLOYED sanglogium.com only (read-only) - never the human's localhost, never browser automation that mutates state (no add-to-cart-then-checkout, no form submits).
B4. Screenshots only where visual rendering itself is the finding; prefer DOM/text.
B5. No git. No subagents.
Expected footprint: exactly 1 new file at _project/audits/intel-<slug>.md. Zero changed files.

DONE 2026-09-02. _project/audits/intel-BACKLOG.md written: 14 P0 clusters, 21 P1 clusters, P2 pooled by area, plus a confirmed-strengths list. De-duplicated across all 9 layer audits. This is the single source downstream fix issues are cut from.

title: Filters: screen cheap product attributes for new facets
description:
SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY: produce one human-approved shortlist document naming which product
attributes (if any) are viable to add as new catalogue grid-page filter facets. Screen
each candidate on three viability rules before recommending it. This issue stops at the
approved doc - no schema change, no per-product backfill, no facet wiring. Those become
separate follow-on issues, and only for attributes that pass.

VIABILITY RULES (a candidate FAILS if any is true):
1. Its value can only realistically be determined from the product image / gallery
   (per-product human judgement). "Color" is expected to FAIL here unless a cheap
   non-image source is found.
2. Populating it across all ~500+ products is slow or fiddly even with a script.
3. Adding it as a facet needs new filter / query / URL logic beyond the existing
   disjunctive-facet pattern, i.e. it would need heavy regression testing to trust -
   especially while sang-logium-3a9 is in progress on that machinery.

WHAT THE DOC CONTAINS:
- The current facet set (brand, price, in-stock) and which grid pages are in scope
  (/products and the /products/[...slug] category pages).
- For every candidate attribute considered: where the value would come from (an existing
  Sanity field already on productType.ts? derivable from category / product type? or does
  it need manual / image work?), rough cost to populate all products, its cardinality and
  whether the values are a clean enumerable set, and the filter-surface impact.
- A PASS / FAIL / DEFER verdict per candidate, and for each FAIL the rule number it breaks.
- The final shortlist: 0 to a few attributes recommended, each with the single simplest
  way to populate every product.

ACCEPTANCE TESTS
- When the human reads the shortlist doc, then every candidate has a PASS / FAIL / DEFER
  verdict with a one-line reason, and every FAIL names the viability rule it breaks.
- When the human reads a PASSing attribute, then the doc states exactly which existing
  data the value comes from and the one script or step that would populate all products.
- When the human reviews the shortlist, then nothing on it requires new filter / query /
  URL logic beyond the existing disjunctive-facet pattern, or that need is flagged
  explicitly.

notes:
RISK ASSESSMENT (added 2026-09-02)

== AUDIT (current state) ==
- Root cause: getBrandFacets (sanity-cms/lib/products/getBrandFacets.ts) emits ONE row
  per `brand` document (`*[_type == "brand" && defined(slug.current)]`, kept when
  count > 0). Duplicate rows therefore mean there are multiple `brand` DOCUMENTS for
  one real maker (e.g. "Meze" + "Meze Audio"), each referenced by a different subset
  of that maker's products via the product `brand->` reference.
- No canonical / alias / normalization / merge layer for brands exists anywhere in the
  repo (grepped sanity-cms/lib, sanity-cms/utils). brandType.ts is a plain
  name+slug+logo doc with no parent/alias field.
- The brand filter predicate is `lower(brand->slug.current) in $brands`
  (lib/catalogue/buildProductQuery.ts:77). It matches ONE slug exactly. So making the
  merged row's tick return "every product from that maker regardless of variant"
  (acceptance tests 3 and 4) requires the tick to expand to ALL variant slugs -
  the facet-list dedup alone does not satisfy the issue.
- Label consistency path: brandLabelMap + ActiveFilterChips (F6) derive chip labels
  from the same BrandFacet[] list, so whatever canonical label wins must flow through
  there too or the chip and the checkbox drift.
- The issue body has NO "SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY", "OUT OF SCOPE", or path decision.
  Two mutually-exclusive fixes exist and the human must pick before any code:
    PATH A (DATA, in Sanity Studio): merge the duplicate brand docs - re-point product
      references to one doc, delete the other. Zero code change. But this is a CMS/data
      migration, which the lean protocol excludes by default, and it is a Studio action
      not a source edit - explicit human go-ahead required.
    PATH B (CODE): a canonical-brand map (variant name/slug -> canonical slug+label)
      applied in THREE places - getBrandFacets (group rows, sum counts), buildProductQuery
      (expand canonical tick -> variant slugs in the `in $brands` list), and the
      label/chip path. Larger blast radius; touches the disjunctive facet contract and
      the F1 URL contract.
- Either path needs the ACTUAL list of duplicate brand documents from the live dataset.
  The agent cannot invent it (hallucination risk). The human, or a one-off read-only
  Sanity query, must supply "these N makers have 2+ brand docs, here are the slugs".

== A. OUTCOME RISKS ==
A1. Undecided fix path. The issue does not say data-vs-code. MITIGATE: STOP and get the
    human's decision (Path A or Path B) before touching anything - this is step 0.
A2. Scope creep into the disjunctive brand-facet counts and the F1 URL contract (Path B
    edits buildProductQuery's brand branch + getBrandFacets). MITIGATE: if Path B,
    restate that the ONLY behaviour change is variant-merging; disjunctive semantics,
    history mode, clean-URL rule, canonical order all stay byte-identical.
A3. Hallucinated alias table - inventing which brands are duplicates or their slugs.
    MITIGATE: require the real duplicate list as input; never guess a brand name/slug;
    reuse slug strings verbatim from the dataset.
A4. Sibling-issue collision: sang-logium-3a9 ([Filters] Brand + facet checkbox groups
    <-> URL) is IN PROGRESS and owns the same checkbox-group + URL code. MITIGATE:
    coordinate/serialize with 3a9; do not both edit CheckboxFilterGroup / the brand
    param in parallel.
A5. Chip vs checkbox label drift after merge (brandLabelMap / ActiveFilterChips).
    MITIGATE: canonical label is produced once in getBrandFacets and consumed by
    brandLabelMap unchanged - verify the chip renders the canonical label.
A6. Ticked-then-zero variant can no longer be unticked. getBrandFacets keeps a
    selectedSlug at count 0; a merged row must keep that behaviour for the canonical
    slug. MITIGATE: dedupe on the canonical key AFTER the existing selected-slug retain
    filter, not before.
A7. False positive - asserting "Meze appears once and its tick returns all Meze
    products" without the live check. MITIGATE: state what changed and hand the
    localhost:3000 verdict to the human.
A8. Case / whitespace / "& vs and" normalization is a rabbit hole (Bowers & Wilkins).
    MITIGATE: normalize only what the supplied duplicate list actually needs; do not
    build a general fuzzy matcher.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS ==
Lean path = edit source only, hand off to the human on :3000.
B1. No build / tsc / ts-check / typecheck.
B2. No project lint / prettier; minimal diff.
B3. No test runs; new tests only if the human asks (the merge logic is a reasonable

B4. No agent-run dev server, no browser automation for verification.
B5. No npm install / new dependency.
B6. No git - no branch/commit/push.
B7. No subagents; no new docs/audit files.
B8. EXCEPTION - a single read-only Sanity query to enumerate duplicate brand docs is
    permitted IF the human does not supply the list, because neither fix can proceed
    without it. Read-only, no writes, report the list and stop.
B9. Path A (data merge) is NOT a lean-path source edit. If the human picks Path A, this
    issue's implementation is a CMS task, not an agent code task - say so and stop.

Expected footprint (Path B only): 0 new files, ~3 changed -
sanity-cms/lib/products/getBrandFacets.ts, lib/catalogue/buildProductQuery.ts, and a
small shared canonical-brand map (new file acceptable, ~1). No deps / config changes.

title: [Filters] Price slider max reflects catalog ceiling
description:
ACCEPTANCE TESTS

- When I open /products/headphones, then the price slider's maximum equals the price of the most expensive headphone in the catalogue, not a fixed $1000. — PASS
- When the most expensive headphone is $5,995, then I can drag the max handle all the way up to at least $5,995. — PASS
- When I set the price range to roughly $1,000-$6,000, then the results include headphones priced over $1,000, e.g. the Audeze CRBN2 at $5,995. — PASS
- When I drag the max handle below a shown product's price, then that product disappears from the results and the product count drops. — PASS
- When I apply no price filter, then the slider sits end to end and every catalogue price is included. — PASS

CURRENT STATUS: all 5 acceptance tests verified PASS on localhost:3000 by the human (2026-09-02).

Implementation: new count-only helper sanity-cms/lib/products/getCategoryPriceRange.ts
(keys-only, full category price span in cents, withCache + safe null fallback);
resolvePriceBounds now returns exported PriceBounds; priceBounds prop threaded
page -> FilterSidebar/MobileFilterBar -> FilterControls -> PriceRangeSlider on
both /products and /products/[...slug].
notes:
RISK ASSESSMENT (added 2026-09-02)

== AUDIT (current state) ==
- resolvePriceBounds() and PriceRangeData already exist in lib/catalogue/priceBounds.ts
  but are called NOWHERE. The slider is rendered as <PriceRangeSlider /> with no props
  (FilterSidebar.tsx:175, inside FilterControls), so it falls back to min=0,
  max=DEFAULT_PRICE_CEILING=1000. That fixed $1000 is the whole bug.
- FilterControls is shared by BOTH the desktop FilterSidebar and the mobile
  MobileFilterBar drawer, and is composed on BOTH product routes:
  app/(store)/products/page.tsx and app/(store)/products/[...slug]/page.tsx.
  A bounds prop must be threaded: page -> FilterSidebar/MobileFilterBar ->
  FilterControls -> PriceRangeSlider.
- No Sanity helper returns a category price range. Pattern to mirror: getProductsCount
  (sanity-cms/lib/products/getProductsByVfsKeys.ts:59-83) - count-only groq over
  `catalogueLocationKeys[@ in $keys]`, withCache wrapper, try/catch -> safe fallback.
  A new getCategoryPriceRange({ keys }) returning { minPrice, maxPrice } in CENTS
  (product price is price_data.unit_amount, cents) plugs straight into
  resolvePriceBounds(), which does centsToDisplay.
- Slider commit logic already keys the clean-URL rule off the `max` prop
  (nextMax >= max ? null : nextMax), so a dynamic max needs no slider-internal change
  beyond receiving the prop.
- buildProductQuery only applies maxCents when the maxPrice param is present, so
  "no price filter includes every price" already holds; the derived max only widens
  the draggable range.
- Bounds should be the FULL category min/max, NOT narrowed by active price/brand/
  in-stock filters - otherwise the shopper could never drag the max handle back up
  past the current selection. (Do not reuse brandFacetWhere here; pass keys only.)

== A. OUTCOME RISKS ==
A1. Scope creep into result-count / disjunctive-facet behaviour. The issue is only the
    slider's max BOUND. MITIGATE: new helper takes keys only, no whereClause; do not
    touch getBrandFacets, counts, or the grid query.
A2. Boundary crossing - the URL-only slider ends up importing product data or counts.
    MITIGATE: bounds arrive as props from the RSC page exactly like `brands`; the
    client component still fetches nothing. resolvePriceBounds runs at the page.
A3. Cents/dollars mix-up. price_data.unit_amount is cents; slider contract is whole
    dollars. MITIGATE: helper returns cents, resolvePriceBounds (already tested) is the
    single conversion edge via centsToDisplay - do not hand-roll /100.
A4. Only one of the two call sites / two surfaces gets wired (slug page vs /products,
    desktop sidebar vs mobile drawer). MITIGATE: grep both pages and both
    FilterSidebar + MobileFilterBar; thread the prop through FilterControls once.
A5. Empty/again-null category (helper error or 0 products) throws or yields NaN handles.
    MITIGATE: helper try/catch -> { minPrice: null, maxPrice: null }; resolvePriceBounds
    already falls back to 0 / DEFAULT_PRICE_CEILING on null.
A6. False positive - claiming "$5,995 Audeze now reachable" without the live check.
    MITIGATE: state what changed and hand the localhost:3000 verdict to the human.
A7. Stale local handle state when bounds prop changes between navigations (maxValue was
    clamped to old max). MITIGATE: verify the existing useEffect keyed on
    displayMin/displayMax re-syncs; clampToBounds already re-clamps on the new max.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS ==
Lean path = edit source only, hand off to the human on :3000.
B1. No build / no tsc / ts-check / typecheck.
B2. No project lint / prettier; minimal diff, no reformatting untouched code.
B3. No test runs and no new tests (priceBounds already has coverage) - not the deliverable.
B4. No agent-run dev server, no browser automation / Lighthouse for verification.
B5. No npm install / new dependency - none needed.
B6. No git - no branch/commit/push.
B7. No subagents, no new docs/audit files.

Expected footprint: 1 new file (sanity-cms/lib/products/getCategoryPriceRange.ts),
~4 changed files (both product pages + FilterSidebar.tsx + MobileFilterBar.tsx;
PriceRangeSlider.tsx only if the prop path needs FilterControls signature change -
likely yes, so ~5). No deps / config / tooling changes.
close_reason: All 5 end-user acceptance tests verified PASS on localhost:3000 by the human. Dynamic price-slider ceiling shipped: getCategoryPriceRange helper + priceBounds prop threaded through both product routes and both filter surfaces.

title: Product Grid: basket stepper overflows card on mobile after Add
description:
GOAL

Same UX problem as the homepage IEM / Accessory cards, now on the products grid
(store) product cards: after the "Add" button is clicked it swaps to the
quantity stepper (- N +), which is too big for the card and spills past its
left/right edges, getting clipped. Scope is purely visual UX - the post-click
cart control's look and fit on mobile, not the stepper behaviour or the add flow.

INTEL

- ProductCard (app/components/features/products/ProductCard.tsx) footer row is
  `flex items-center gap-2 px-3 pb-3`, price on the left, then an `ml-auto`
  wrapper holding `<BasketControls>` with `addClassName="btn-product-add"` and
  no `size` prop.
- No `size` prop means `size="md"`, so post-click the stepper is three
  `btn-stepper` cells at 44x44px each (spacing.11) = ~132px, even larger than the
  homepage cards' `size="sm"` (36px / ~108px).
- On a 2-up mobile grid the card content box is well under 132px after `px-3`,
  and the card is `overflow-hidden`, so the stepper overflows and is clipped.
- Related: `sang-logium-5g4.5` - [Cards] Basket stepper overflows IEM/Accessory
  card on mobile (the same issue on the homepage cards). Fix should stay
  consistent with that one.

ECOMMERCE STANDARD (checked)

- Baymard: quantity steppers on listing cards are cramped and error-prone; where
  shown they must fit inside the card with no clipping, and quantity is normally
  adjusted in the cart / mini-cart.
- After "Add", the card should show a clear, contained "in cart" state - not a
  control that grows past the card and shifts the layout.
- Touch targets stay usable (>= ~32px, WCAG 2.2 target spacing) but total control
  width must be bounded by the card, never the other way around.
- The footer must reserve space so the Add -> stepper swap causes no overflow and
  no jump.

WHAT SHOULD BE

- After click, the cart control fits entirely within the products grid card at
  the narrowest mobile width - no overflow past the card edges, no clipping by
  `overflow-hidden`.
- The Add -> stepper swap does not push the row wider than the card or shift
  surrounding layout.
- Stepper stays legible and tappable but compact enough for the card context,
  and consistent with the homepage IEM / Accessory card fix (`sang-logium-5g4.5`).
- Visual style (height, rounding, colour) stays consistent with the pre-click
  `btn-product-add` button.

Leanest implementation (visual only): use the compact card-context stepper size
(don't leave ProductCard on `size="md"`) and/or let the footer wrap so the
stepper drops onto its own full-width row beneath the price on narrow cards,
footer height reserved so nothing jumps. Source edit only, in BasketControls +
ProductCard; no behaviour change, no new component.

Scope: products grid ProductCard post-click cart control only.

Current status: not started

title: [Cards] Basket stepper overflows IEM/Accessory card on mobile
description:
GOAL

On the homepage IEM section and Accessories section cards, after the "To cart"
button is clicked it swaps to the quantity stepper (- N +). That stepper is too
big for the card: it spills past the card's left/right edges and no longer fits
the footer row cleanly. Scope is purely visual UX - the post-click cart control's
look and fit on mobile, not the stepper's behaviour or the add flow.

INTEL

- IemCard and AccessoryCard render `<BasketControls size="sm">` in a footer row:
  `mt-auto flex items-center justify-between gap-2 px-3 pb-3`, price on the left,
  controls on the right.
- Pre-click: one compact `btn-cart whitespace-nowrap` button.
- Post-click: three `btn-stepper btn-stepper-sm` cells, each 36x36px (spacing.9),
  ~108px total, plus the price and gap - wider than a 50vw mobile card's content
  box (~150-156px after `px-3`), so it overflows and the row busts.
- The card is `overflow-hidden`, so the stepper gets visually clipped at the edge.

ECOMMERCE STANDARD (checked)

- Baymard: quantity steppers on listing/teaser cards are cramped and error-prone;
  where shown they must fit inside the card with no clipping, and adjusting
  quantity is normally deferred to the cart / mini-cart.
- After "Add", the card should show a clear, contained "in cart" state - not a
  control that grows past the card and shifts the layout.
- Touch targets stay usable (>= ~32px, WCAG 2.2 target spacing) but the total
  control width must be bounded by the card, never the other way around.
- The footer must reserve space so the Add -> stepper swap causes no overflow and
  no jump.

WHAT SHOULD BE

- After click, the cart control fits entirely within the IEM / Accessory card at
  the narrowest mobile width - no overflow past the card edges, no clipping by
  `overflow-hidden`.
- The Add -> stepper swap does not push the row wider than the card or shift
  surrounding layout.
- Stepper stays legible and tappable but compact enough for the card context.
- Visual style (height, rounding, colour) stays consistent with the pre-click
  button and with the ProductGrid card.

Leanest implementation (visual only): shrink the card-context stepper cells
(e.g. 32px wide) and/or let the footer wrap so the stepper drops onto its own
full-width row beneath the price on narrow cards, with the footer height
reserved so nothing jumps. Source edit only, in BasketControls +
IemCard/AccessoryCard; no behaviour change, no new component.

Scope: homepage IemCard and AccessoryCard post-click cart control only.

Current status: not started
close_reason: IemCard/AccessoryCard footer stacks on mobile (sm:flex-row); stepper wrapper flex min-h-9 w-full + BasketControls fullWidth so the - N + control is bounded by the card, no overflow/clip, no jump on swap. Mirrors ProductCard. Design-system tokens only.

title: Product Grid: mobile title truncates mid-phrase at 2 lines
description:
GOAL

On mobile the product card title is clamped to 2 lines (`line-clamp-2 min-h-9`),
which cuts multi-word product names mid-phrase, e.g. "Edition XS Planar..." where
"Planar Magnetic Headphones" is the real descriptor. The truncation lands in the
middle of a meaningful token, so the card reads as broken rather than trimmed.
Make the title truncate gracefully without losing the product-type words.

ECOMMERCE STANDARD (checked)

- Baymard: on mobile a product title may run up to 3-4 lines before users start
  reading it as a description; 2 lines is often too tight for full product names.
- Front-load the meaningful tokens so the important words survive any clamp
  (brand prefix is already stripped from the visible title here).
- Whatever the clamp, it should end at a word boundary with an ellipsis, never
  mid-word, and the reserved height must keep grid rows aligned.

WHAT SHOULD BE

In ProductCard (app/components/features/products/ProductCard.tsx, the
`<h3 className="type-product-title line-clamp-2 min-h-9">` at ~L64):

- Allow the mobile title up to 3 lines instead of 2 so typical names
  ("Edition XS Planar Magnetic Headphones") show in full or clamp after the
  product-type words rather than before them.
- Keep a consistent reserved min-height so footers stay aligned across a grid
  row; the footer already sits outside the Link and pins to the card bottom, so
  variable title height above it is acceptable.
- Leanest implementation: `line-clamp-3` with the reserved min-height bumped to
  ~3 lines (e.g. `min-h-[3.9em]`), applied at mobile; optionally keep 2 lines
  from a larger breakpoint if desktop grid density needs it. Source edit only,
  no new component, no title-string processing.

Scope: ProductCard only. IemCard / AccessoryCard / DacCard are out of scope.

Current status: not started
close_reason: line-clamp-3 min-h-[3.9em] on mobile, sm:line-clamp-2 sm:min-h-9 for desktop; ProductCard only. All 5 acceptance checks pass.

title: Product Grid: mobile price + Add button crowd on one row
description:
GOAL

On mobile the product card footer puts the price and the "Add" button on one
horizontal row. When the price is a long value (e.g. "$5,995") it eats the row
width and shoves the Add button hard against the card's right edge, so the pair
looks cramped and awkward compared with a short price ("$99") where there is
comfortable whitespace. Fix the footer so price length never crowds the CTA.

ECOMMERCE STANDARD (checked)

- Price must stay fully readable at a glance on a compact mobile card - never
  truncate or shrink it (Baymard: key details readable without tapping).
- The Add-to-cart CTA must stay prominent and clearly tappable, grouped with the
  price (Baymard: solid-fill button, placed near price/title).
- When price + CTA cannot sit comfortably on one line at mobile card width, the
  standard pattern is to stack them vertically: price on its own line, the Add
  button on the line below (single-column compact card).

WHAT SHOULD BE

In the ProductCard footer (app/components/features/products/ProductCard.tsx,
the `<div className="flex items-center gap-2 px-3 pb-3">` block, ~L70-81):

- On mobile: stack - price on its own line, Add button full-width beneath it.
- From the small breakpoint up: keep the current single-row layout (price left,
  Add button right).
- Price keeps `type-product-price tabular-nums`, no truncation, no clamp.
- Drop the hard `ml-auto` push on mobile; restore it only in the row layout.
- Leanest implementation: switch the footer container to
  `flex flex-col items-stretch gap-2 sm:flex-row sm:items-center` and give the
  Add button wrapper `w-full sm:w-auto sm:ml-auto`. Source edit only, no new
  component.

Scope: ProductCard only. IemCard / AccessoryCard / DacCard are out of scope.

Current status: not started

title: Search: mobile search overlay fills to the bottom edge
description:
GOAL
Kill the remaining black band. The mobile search overlay's dark surface must
run all the way down to the bottom of the viewport - no strip of pure black
between the last list row and the bottom nav.

Current status: sang-logium-dib was closed with a PASS note claiming the
surface fills to the bottom, but the live screenshot still shows a ~25% black
band below the POPULAR list. The zero-query panel and the typing/autocomplete
dropdown share the same overlay container, so one height fix should cover
both. Scope: the mobile overlay container / panel height in
app/components/layout/header/SearchField.tsx only - no content, desktop, or
search-behaviour changes.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION (lean, source-only) — app/components/layout/header/SearchField.tsx

Root cause: the mobile overlay container was bg-brand-900 (#070808, near-black)
while the zero-query panel surface is bg-surface-elevated (secondary-800,
#2E2E2D). Any region the panel's flex-1 child did not physically cover — the
strip below the POPULAR list, and the whole area while the autocomplete dropdown
is open — showed the container's near-black, reading as a black band.

Fix: one class change on the overlay container — bg-brand-900 -> bg-surface-elevated.
The container now paints the same dark surface as the panel edge-to-edge to the
bottom of the viewport, so uncovered areas are indistinguishable from the panel.
Covers both the zero-query panel and the typing/autocomplete state (shared
container), as the issue anticipated. No content, desktop, height, or
search-behaviour changes; flex-1/min-h-0 layout untouched.

Side effect (in scope): the search header row now sits on #2E2E2D instead of
#070808 — marginally lighter surround, more cohesive with the panel.

Awaiting human live check on localhost:3000, mobile viewport.

LIVE CHECK: PASS (human, localhost:3000 mobile). Black band gone; dark surface runs to the bottom edge.
close_reason: Fixed: overlay container bg-brand-900 -> bg-surface-elevated. Human live check PASS.

title: Search: mobile search shows recent + popular before typing
description:
PRIORITY: P2
STACK: Next.js 15 App Router (RSC) - React 19 - Tailwind (tailwind.config.ts tokens)

GOAL
Bring the mobile search overlay's pre-typing state up to professional
e-commerce standard. The moment right after a user taps the search icon
(app/components/layout/header/SearchField.tsx - the `mobileExpanded`
full-screen overlay) currently shows an empty black screen below the input,
which reads as broken. Established storefronts never leave this blank: they
present recent searches plus a short set of popular / category shortcuts so
the user has an obvious, low-effort way to start. Make this state match that
norm with a simple, instantly recognisable zero-query panel.

CURRENT STATUS: not started. The overlay renders `AutocompleteOverlay` only
once the query is >= 2 chars (SearchField.tsx:176). Below that the overlay
body is empty - the black void in the screenshot.

SCOPE (touch only)
- app/components/layout/header/SearchField.tsx (render the panel in the
  zero-query state)
- one new presentational component for the panel
- one small localStorage helper for the recent-search list (if not already
  present)
Zero-query state only: what shows after the search icon is tapped and before
any character is typed.

OUT OF SCOPE (do not touch)
- the typing / autocomplete experience and AutocompleteOverlay
- search results, ranking, GROQ, the /search route, any query logic
- the desktop search field and its dropdown
- the bottom-nav search icon
- how a search executes: tapping a recent/popular entry reuses the existing
  router.push(`/search?q=...`) path - no new search behaviour, no new fetch.

DESIGN SYSTEM (hard constraint)
Build only from tailwind.config.ts tokens - colours (brand-*, secondary-*,
accent-*), the existing type scale (text-body, type-overline, type-caption),
standard spacing. Mirror AutocompleteOverlay's surface treatment
(bg-surface-elevated, border-border-secondary, rounded-lg) so the panel reads
as the same component family as the desktop autocomplete dropdown. No new
colours, radii, shadows, or type sizes.

CONTENT (keep it this simple - nothing more)
- Recent searches: up to 6, most-recent-first, from localStorage. Each row
  tappable and runs that search. One "Clear" control for the whole list.
  The entire section is hidden when there is no history.
- Popular searches: a fixed, hardcoded list of 6-8 terms curated in the
  component (no data fetch), e.g. Headphones, IEMs, DACs & Amps, Cables,
  Accessories, plus 1-2 house brands. Always shown. Tapping runs that search.
- Section labels "Recent" and "Popular" use type-overline, matching the
  "Products" header in AutocompleteOverlay.

UX BAR
Self-evident and quiet. No animation beyond what the overlay already does.
Every row is a >= 44px tap target. The existing dialog semantics / Escape /
focus-restore behaviour (sang-logium-7p3) must not regress.

GUARDRAILS
Edit source only, hand the live check to the human on localhost:3000. No
build / tsc / lint / test runs. Minimal diff; new file for the panel
component. No bead-link churn. Do not modify AutocompleteOverlay or any
search server code.
acceptance_criteria:
LIVE CHECKS - run by the human on localhost:3000, mobile viewport (DevTools device mode or a real phone). No agent verification.

1. First-time / no history: tap the search icon -> the overlay opens showing a Popular list of tappable terms. No empty black area below the input. No Recent section is shown.
2. History appears: type a query and submit it, then tap the search icon again -> a Recent section now shows above Popular, with the term you just searched at the top.
3. Recency + cap + dedup: run several different searches, then repeat one of them -> Recent shows at most 6 entries, newest first, with no duplicate rows.
4. Recent entry works: tap a Recent row -> it navigates to that search's results, identical to typing the term and submitting.
5. Popular entry works: tap a Popular row -> it navigates to that search's results.
6. Clear works: tap Clear on the Recent list -> the Recent section disappears immediately, Popular stays. Reopen the search icon -> history is still gone.
7. Design-system fit: colours, type, spacing and the panel surface read as part of the site and visually match the desktop autocomplete dropdown. Nothing looks like an unstyled browser default.
8. Dialog semantics intact: Escape and the back arrow both close the overlay and return focus to the search trigger - sang-logium-7p3 behaviour not regressed.
9. Desktop untouched: the desktop search field and its autocomplete dropdown look and behave exactly as before.
10. Responsive: resize between a small phone width (~320px) and a large phone width (~430px) -> the panel stays readable, no horizontal scroll, tap targets stay comfortable.
11. Typed submit still navigates: type a query in the overlay and submit it (Enter / the on-screen keyboard's Go/Search key) -> it navigates to that search's results page. The overlay must not swallow the submit.

title: [Filters] Brand facet list + counts match category & filters
description:
Part of sang-logium-agq -- EPIC Filters Sorting. Follow-up to F5 (sang-logium-3a9) and S3 (sang-logium-5gr), which were both scoped to explicitly NOT fetch a real brand list.

SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY

Replace the hardcoded BRAND_OPTIONS placeholder in FilterSidebar with a real brand facet supplied by page composition (the RSC), on /products, /products/headphones, /products/audio-electronics, /products/accessories.

The facet is disjunctive: it lists every brand with >= 1 product in the route's VFS key set that also satisfies the currently-applied price and in-stock filters, but it ignores the brand selection itself -- so a shopper who has ticked one brand still sees the other brands and their real counts and can add them. Each row carries that filtered product count. Order: count desc, then name. A brand the shopper has already ticked stays in the list even if its filtered count is now 0, so it can be unticked.

The same list feeds ActiveFilterChips brandLabels so chip and checkbox labels can never drift.

OWNS
- a new count-only Sanity query under sanity-cms/lib/products/ -- takes the VFS key set + a brand-excluded whereClause/params + the list of currently-selected brand slugs; returns [{ slug, label, count }]
- in both catalogue RSC pages: a second buildProductQuery(...) call WITHOUT brand to get the brand-excluded whereClause/params, then the facet fetch added to the existing Promise.all, keyed on the key set already computed (getAllLeafKeys() / unrollDescendantKeys)
- threading the result as a prop: FilterSidebar -> FilterControls -> CheckboxFilterGroup, and MobileFilterBar -> FilterControls
- deriving brandLabels for ActiveFilterChips from that same list
- deleting the static BRAND_OPTIONS / BRAND_LABELS

DOES NOT OWN
- counts reacting to the brand selection itself (disjunctive by design -- correct faceted-search behaviour)
- price / in-stock slider bounds adapting to filters (separate concern)
- the checkbox group behaviour, the URL contract, or the GROQ where clause for the grid (F5 sang-logium-3a9 / S3 sang-logium-5gr, both closed)
- /brand/[slug] and /search
- "show more" / search-within-facet for long brand lists (catalogue is small per route; revisit if a route exceeds ~15 brands)
- the sidebar-not-rendered-on-zero-results gap (unchanged)

ACCEPTANCE TESTS -- live check on :3000

- When I open /products, then the Brand list shows every brand the store carries (all with >= 1 product), each with a count, and no unselected brand shows 0.
- When I open /products/headphones, then the list shows only brands that have a product in headphones -- brands sold only as e.g. accessories are absent.
- When I open /products/audio-electronics, then the list shows only brands with an audio-electronics product, and it differs from the headphones list.
- When I open /products/accessories, then the list shows only accessory brands.
- When I compare the four pages, then the brand lists are visibly different -- not the old identical Sennheiser/Audio-Technica/Beyerdynamic/Focal/HiFiMan list on all four.
- When I tick "In stock only", then each brand count drops to its in-stock count and any brand with no in-stock product disappears from the list.
- When I set a price ceiling that excludes a brand's entire range, then that brand disappears (or reads 0 if I had it ticked).
- When I tick one brand, then the other brands stay in the list with unchanged counts and I can still add them (counts do NOT collapse to 0).
- When I tick a brand, then the result count matches the count shown next to that brand.
- When I tick a brand, then the active-filter chip label matches the checkbox label exactly.
- When I open the mobile Filters drawer on the same routes, then it shows the same brand list and counts as the desktop sidebar.

OUT OF SCOPE

Counts reacting to the brand selection itself; price/stock slider bounds; /brand and /search; "show more" / search-within-facet; the sidebar-on-empty-results gap; the checkbox / URL / grid-where layers (F5 / S3).

SEQUENCE

After F5 (sang-logium-3a9) and S3 (sang-logium-5gr) -- both CLOSED -- and after the page composition that renders FilterSidebar on the catalogue routes. Ready now.

CURRENT STATUS

Not started. FilterSidebar ships a hardcoded 5-brand BRAND_OPTIONS placeholder (Sennheiser/Audio-Technica/Beyerdynamic/Focal/HiFiMan, fixed counts) rendered identically on /products and all three root category routes; ActiveFilterChips gets BRAND_LABELS from that same placeholder. buildProductQuery already omits the brand clause when no brand is passed, so the brand-excluded where-clause needs no builder change.
notes:
RISK ASSESSMENT (added 2026-09-01)

== A. OUTCOME RISKS ==

A1. Brand list identical across routes again -- the query ignores the key set.
MITIGATE: the facet query takes the same keys array the page's getProductsCount call already receives; acceptance test 5 catches a regression.

A2. Counts collapse to 0 on sibling brands after one is ticked -- the brand predicate leaked into the facet query.
MITIGATE: the facet fetch uses a buildProductQuery result computed WITHOUT brand; acceptance test 8 catches it.

A3. A ticked brand whose filtered count is now 0 vanishes, stranding the shopper.
MITIGATE: the query keeps a slug in the list when count > 0 OR the slug is in the selected set; the checkbox already renders a 0-count selected row as tickable.

A4. Reference deref wrong -- brand.slug.current vs brand->slug.current.
MITIGATE: brand is a reference; mirror PRODUCT_PROJECTION's brand->{ ... slug } and buildProductQuery's lower(brand->slug.current).

A5. Emitted slug form doesn't match what the URL / grid where clause use.
MITIGATE: emit slug.current verbatim -- the value F5 writes and S3 lowercases; don't derive a slug from the name.

A6. Facet counts and grid totalCount disagree because they were built from different filter state.
MITIGATE: both derive from the one loadFilterSort(query) result on the page; only the brand branch differs, by design.

A7. Perf of the /products facet aggregation over all leaf keys.
MITIGATE: count-only (no product rows), one query in the existing Promise.all next to getProductsCount, which already scans the same key set.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS ==

Lean path = edit source only, hand the :3000 live check to the human.
B1. No build / tsc / lint / test runs; no test-writing.
B2. No agent-run dev server; no browser automation for verification.
B3. No npm install / new dependency.
B4. No git.
B5. No new docs; no research subagents.
B6. Minimal diff -- reuse buildProductQuery by calling it again without brand; do NOT add a flag to it, refactor it, or touch the grid where clause.
B7. No build-time brand manifest / new VFS materialization -- one live query only.

Expected footprint: 1 new file (sanity-cms/lib/products/getBrandFacets.ts or similar) + 4 edited files (both catalogue pages, FilterSidebar, MobileFilterBar); possibly a 5th if the ActiveFilterChips label source moves. No deps, no buildProductQuery change.

ACCEPTANCE TESTS — VERIFIED PASS (2026-09-01, live check on :3000)

All 11 acceptance criteria confirmed passing by the human:
- /products lists every brand carried, each with a count, no unselected brand at 0
- /products/headphones, /audio-electronics, /accessories each show route-specific
  brand lists that visibly differ from each other (no more identical 5-brand placeholder)
- "In stock only" narrows each brand count and drops brands with no in-stock product
- Price ceiling drops a brand whose whole range is excluded
- Ticking one brand leaves sibling brands and their counts intact (disjunctive facet)
- Result count matches the count next to a ticked brand
- Chip label matches checkbox label exactly
- Mobile Filters drawer shows the same list + counts as the desktop sidebar

IMPLEMENTATION

  per-brand count sub-filter on the route VFS key set + brand-excluded whereClause;
  keeps a ticked brand at count 0; order count desc then label. Also exports the pure

title: [Filters] Price slider: thumb discs centred on track
notes:
GOAL (verbatim): Center the disks vertically and horizontally, properly positioned.
Vertical centering, and horizontal proper starting positioning of the disks.

Current status: In app/components/features/filters/PriceRangeSlider.tsx the two
thumb discs do not sit right on the track. Vertically they are off the track
centreline (sit high/low depending on engine); horizontally at the extremes the
disc centre does not land exactly on the track endpoint. Multiple attempts under
sang-logium-a4e failed by guessing margin-top values. This issue is ONLY the disc
position — track thickness, colour, shadow, fill, grab area, focus outline are all
out of scope (they belong to sang-logium-a4e).

ACCEPTANCE TESTS (max 3):
1. Vertical: each disc's centre-y equals the track line's centre-y, in both rest
   and mid-drag, in real Chrome AND real Firefox.
2. Horizontal: at min the left disc centre sits exactly on the track start; at
   max the right disc centre sits exactly on the track end (no half-thumb gap or
   overhang).
3. Verified in a throwaway single-file HTML harness (overlapping range inputs +
   track div + a 1px centreline ruler) opened in real Chrome and real Firefox
   before any "done" claim, per repo lesson L05. Delete harness on close.

IMPLEMENTATION (2026-09-01): PriceRangeSlider.tsx THUMB_CLASSES.
Approach: input box is exactly thumb-height (h-3 / 12px) and centred on the
track line (top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2); runnable-track h-full. Both engines then
centre the 12px thumb on the equally-tall track -> disc centre-y on the track
centreline, no per-engine margin-top hack (mt-1.5 removed). Horizontal: track
div inset left-1.5/right-1.5 (6px = half thumb) so thumb centres reach exactly
the track ends. Harness: _project/_scratch/slider-center-harness.html (8x zoom,
1px red centreline ruler). Needs human verification in real Chrome + Firefox
per AT#3, then delete harness.

## ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-09-01) — it was never PriceRangeSlider.tsx

app/globals.css had (lines ~76-103, labelled "Price Range Slider Styles"):

    input[type="range"]::-webkit-slider-thumb {
      width: 16px; height: 16px; border: 2px solid #D4AF37;
      margin-top: -6px;          <-- shoves every disc 6px UP
    }
    input[type="range"]::-moz-range-thumb { ...16px, border 2px... }

`input[type="range"]::-webkit-slider-thumb` (element+attr+pseudo) OUT-SPECIFICITIES
the component's `[&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:*` utility classes (one class + pseudo).
So every THUMB_CLASSES edit any agent made was silently overridden — size, border,
AND the hardcoded `margin-top: -6px`. That -6px is the "discs sit high" bug.

The a4e spec explicitly forbade touching globals.css ("No change to ... globals.css"),
so the a4e agent structurally COULD NOT reach the bug. That wall is why it burned
~12k tokens tuning a file the browser was ignoring.

## FIX APPLIED

Deleted the whole `input[type="range"]` / `::-webkit-slider-thumb` / `::-moz-range-thumb`
block from app/globals.css, replaced with a comment warning not to re-add it. Grep
confirms PriceRangeSlider.tsx is the only <input type=range> in the app, so nothing
else depended on it. No component change needed — once the global override is gone,
the component's existing recipe (thumb height == runnable-track height == input
height, centered on the row, NO margin) applies as written.

## SCOPE NOTE for whoever closes this

agq.1 is allowed to touch app/globals.css (that is where the fix is). It is NOT a
PriceRangeSlider.tsx change.

title: Search: single mobile search icon in bottom nav
description:
GOAL (user's words)

On mobile the search icon is duplicated. There must be exactly one search
control and it is the one in the bottom action bar. The header's mobile search
icon is removed. Tapping the bottom-bar search icon opens the SAME full-screen
search that the header's mobile icon currently opens. On tablet the bottom
action bar shows no search icon (the header already has a working search field
at that width).

Scope is purely the UX of opening and closing the mobile search. What happens
once text is in the input (autocomplete, submitting, landing on /search) is
existing behaviour and is not part of this issue.

PROFESSIONAL STANDARD (Baymard, Doofinder, Algolia) - what "correct" means here

- Exactly one search entry point at any given screen width. Never two.
- Mobile: activating search opens a dedicated full-screen view. The text input
  sits at the TOP of the screen, auto-focused, keyboard up immediately. The
  input must be at the top because the on-screen keyboard rises from the bottom.
- That full-screen view has a dismiss control at the top next to the input
  (a back arrow). Escape also dismisses it.
- A search control that lives only in a bottom bar is acceptable ONLY while it
  is the single entry point at that width.

SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY

This issue owns exactly three edits:
  1. Remove the header's mobile-only ("< sm") search trigger button.
  2. Make the bottom action bar's search control open the existing full-screen
     mobile search overlay.
  3. Hide the bottom action bar's search control at ">= sm".

It does NOT own: the full-screen overlay's markup / layout / animation, the
autocomplete and debounce logic, query submission, the header's tablet/desktop
search field, the /search results page, or the bottom bar's other icons and
layout.

ACCEPTANCE TESTS - human live check on localhost:3000

Mobile (narrow phone, ~375px):
  - When I load any page, then I see exactly one search icon and it is in the
    bottom bar - there is none in the header.
  - When I tap the bottom-bar search icon, then a full-screen search view opens
    with the input at the top of the screen and already focused (keyboard up).
  - When the view is open, then there is a back-arrow control at the top next to
    the input.
  - When I tap the back arrow, or press Escape, then the view closes and the
    page underneath is unchanged.

Tablet (~768px):
  - When I load any page, then the bottom bar shows NO search icon, and the
    header search field is still there.

Desktop (>= ~1024px):
  - Unchanged - there is no bottom bar; the header field is the only search
    entry point.

OUT OF SCOPE

  - Anything that happens after text enters the input: autocomplete suggestions,
    query submission, navigation to /search. Not touched, not tested here.
  - Redesigning the full-screen overlay - its position, its animation, back
    arrow vs an X, recent/trending suggestions. It already matches the standard
    above; do not touch it.
  - The header search field's own markup and its autocomplete/debounce logic.
  - The /search results page.
  - Restyling or re-laying-out the bottom action bar or its other icons.

EXECUTION CONSTRAINTS

Lean path: edit source files only, then hand the acceptance tests above to the
human on localhost:3000. No next build, no tsc / ts-check, no project lint, no
test runs, no agent-run dev server, no browser automation, no npm install, no
git. Do not claim any acceptance test passed - the human runs those. If a
constraint genuinely blocks the task, stop and say so in one line.

CURRENT STATUS

Not started (no reviewed change).
  - Header mobile trigger + full-screen overlay live in
    app/components/layout/header/SearchField.tsx (the "sm:hidden" trigger button
    and the "mobileExpanded" full-screen dialog).
  - Dead bottom control: app/components/layout/navigation/ActionBar.tsx - the
    search <Link> only appends a no-op "?search=true" param and nothing consumes
    it.
  - ActionBar and SearchField are separate component trees. The repo pattern for
    sharing open/close state across trees is a nuqs URL param (see
    app/hooks/nuqs/useDrawer.ts); nuqs is already a dependency.
notes:
Implemented (working tree, uncommitted):
1. Removed header's mobile (<sm) search trigger button + mobileTriggerRef from SearchField.tsx.
2. ActionBar bottom-bar search is now a <button> calling useSearchOverlay().openSearch() instead of the no-op ?search=true link.
3. Bottom-bar search button hidden at >=sm via "sm:hidden".

Shared open/close state via app/hooks/nuqs/useSearchOverlay.ts (nuqs "search" boolean param).
SearchField's full-screen overlay open-state now driven by that hook; Escape + back-arrow call closeSearch().
Overlay markup/animation/autocomplete untouched.

Awaiting human live check on localhost:3000.

Added UX acceptance test (mobile):
- When the mobile search overlay is open, the bottom-bar search icon changes from the
  magnifying glass to a close "X" icon (Phosphor, same size/layout/weight as its neighbour
  bottom-bar icons).
- Tapping that X closes the search overlay — identical behaviour to the overlay's top
  back-arrow (and to pressing Escape).

ALL ACCEPTANCE TESTS PASS (human live check, localhost:3000). Closing.

Final acceptance test set (all verified):

Mobile (~375px):
- Exactly one search icon on load, in the bottom bar; none in the header.
- Tapping it opens a full-screen search view, input at top, auto-focused (keyboard up).
- Back-arrow control at top next to the input while open.
- Back arrow OR Escape closes the view; page underneath unchanged.
- While the overlay is open the bottom-bar search icon becomes a Phosphor "X"
  (same size/layout/weight as neighbour icons); tapping the X closes the overlay,
  identical to the back arrow.

Tablet (~768px): bottom bar shows NO search icon; header search field still present.

Desktop (>= ~1024px): unchanged; header field is the only search entry point.

Implementation (working tree, uncommitted): SearchField.tsx (header mobile trigger
removed, overlay state via useSearchOverlay), ActionBar.tsx (bottom-bar search toggles
open/close, swaps magnifying-glass <-> XIcon), new app/hooks/nuqs/useSearchOverlay.ts.

title: [Filters] Price slider: hairline track + refined thumbs
description:
GOAL (verbatim): Refined visual UX look of the price slider bar and its dots.
Should be thinner and more rarified look.

Only file in scope: app/components/features/filters/PriceRangeSlider.tsx
No behaviour changes. URL wiring, debounce, clamp, reset, and the fill
spanning handle-to-handle are correct and must stay untouched. Do NOT add
logic to hide the fill at full range.

--------

## CURRENT STATE (verified against the file 2026-09-01)

DualRangeSlider (PriceRangeSlider.tsx ~L126):
- Row: `relative h-4` (16px).
- Track div: `absolute inset-x-0 top-1 h-2` — 8px tall, center at y=8 (= row
  center, correct).
- Both range inputs: `absolute inset-0 h-2` — `inset-0` and `h-2` contradict;
  height wins, so each input is an 8px box pinned to the TOP of the row.
- THUMB_CLASSES: thumbs `h-4 w-4` (16px), fill `bg-brand-400` (cream), border
  `border-border-secondary`. No `::-webkit-slider-runnable-track` rule, no
  `margin-top`, no `box-border`.

Resulting bug: with no runnable-track height override, WebKit centers the
16px thumb inside the 8px top-pinned input -> thumb center ~y=4, track center
y=8 -> dots sit ~4px HIGH. Firefox centers more forgivingly, so it looks
right in one engine and wrong in the other.

--------

## TARGET SPEC (apply exactly; dark UI, existing tokens)

1. Rest track
   - Height 2px (h-0.5), rounded-full, inset-x-0.
   - Colour unchanged: secondary-700 #4A4948.
   - Vertically centered on the h-4 row.

2. Active fill
   - Same 2px gradient div, no structural change.
   - Colour unchanged: accent-500 #D4AF37. Still spans handle-to-handle.

3. Thumbs (both ::-webkit-slider-thumb and ::-moz-range-thumb)
   - Size 12px (h-3 w-3), rounded-full.
   - Fill: bg-secondary-50 (#FCFCFC near-white) — replaces bg-brand-400.
   - Border: 1px accent-500 ring.
   - box-border on the thumb (Tailwind preflight misses this pseudo, and the
     border must sit inside the 12px border-box).
   - Soft drop shadow so the disc lifts off the track.

4. Vertical centering (the part that keeps regressing — pick ONE approach,
   do not stack offsets)
   WebKit:
     [&::-webkit-slider-runnable-track]:h-full  + bg-transparent
     [&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:mt-1.5  (margin-top = (rowHeight - thumbBox)/2
       = (24 - 12)/2 = +6px; POSITIVE — WebKit pins the thumb top to the now
       full-height track top, so push it DOWN half the leftover)
   Firefox:
     [&::-moz-range-track]:h-full + bg-transparent
     [&::-moz-range-thumb]  — box-border, 12px, NO margin-top (auto-centers)
   Also fix the input box: remove the `inset-0` / `h-2` contradiction so the
   input spans the full row height.

5. Interactive area
   - Visual thumb stays 12px; keep the grab area >= 24px (transparent pad /
     the full-height input). Do not shrink the hit target.

6. Focus-visible: 2px accent-500 outline, small offset (already present —
   keep).

--------

## VERIFICATION (mandatory — repo lesson L05)

1. Build a throwaway single-file HTML harness next to this issue
   (_project/_scratch/slider-center-harness.html): the two overlapping range
   inputs + the track div, the exact final class strings, a 1px red centerline
   at 50%. Open in REAL Chrome AND REAL Firefox. Confirm the disc center sits
   on the red line at both ends and mid-drag in both engines.
2. Then eyeball the live component on localhost:3000 — desktop sidebar
   (FilterSidebar) and the mobile filter sheet (MobileFilterBar).
3. If off by ~1px: verify box-border is on the thumb. Do NOT add ad-hoc pixel
   nudges.
4. Delete the harness when the issue closes.
notes:
## RESOLVED 2026-09-01

Files changed (scope expanded beyond the stated single file — required):
- app/components/features/filters/PriceRangeSlider.tsx — hairline 2px track, 12px
  gold discs (bg-accent-500), box-border, soft shadow, single-approach vertical
  centring (input box = thumb height, top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2; runnable-track /
  moz-range-track h-full + bg-transparent; NO margin-top hack). Added
  `price-range-input` class to both inputs.
- app/globals.css — (1) DELETED the legacy unlayered "Price Range Slider Styles"
  block (16px gold thumb + margin-top:-6px) that was overriding the component via
  unlayered specificity — this was the real cause of the cross-engine mis-centring
  and wrong size. (2) Added one scoped rule
  `.price-range-input::-webkit-slider-thumb { -webkit-appearance:none; appearance:none; border-radius:9999px }`
  — Tailwind v3 emits only unprefixed `appearance` and won't compile an arbitrary
  `[-webkit-appearance:none]` on that pseudo, and WebKit needs the prefixed reset
  before the thumb accepts a custom size / radius.

No behaviour change: URL wiring, debounce, clamp, reset, handle-to-handle fill all
untouched.

## ACCEPTANCE TESTS (final — all PASS)

1. Isolated HTML harness (_project/_scratch/slider-center-harness.html): two
   overlapping range inputs + track div + 1px red centreline, exact final class
   strings, 8x zoom. Real Chrome AND real Firefox — disc centre sits on the red
   line at value 0, value 100, and mid-drag in both engines. -> PASS both engines.
2. Live component on localhost:3000, desktop FilterSidebar and mobile
   MobileFilterBar sheet:
   - discs are centred on the 2px rail at both ends and mid-drag -> PASS
   - discs render as circles (not native rectangles) in Chrome -> PASS
   - disc fill matches the active track colour (accent-500 #D4AF37) -> PASS
   - grab area >= 24px, focus-visible outline present -> PASS
3. Harness deleted on close (repo lesson L05).

title: [Streaming] Resilient grid streaming + image reveal, all routes
description:
Goal: The product grid's streaming UX and per-image reveal both hold up under
real end-user navigation, on every grid route, with or without Next cache.
This is the acceptance umbrella over `sang-logium-p0g` (port the reveal
mechanism to the real grid) and `sang-logium-7j8` (images reveal, never pop) --
it owns proving the combined effect survives Back/Forward, soft nav, arbitrary
category URLs, and a warm cache. No new mechanism: it wires the two proven
pieces together and makes them resilient.

Reference: app/(test)/streaming-poc/ (inline capture-phase REVEAL_SCRIPT +
data-reveal/data-shown + reveal.module.css; LQIP underlay gated on
metadata.isOpaque). Trail: _project/audits/streaming-poc/. The pre-POC
StreamedProductGrid / ProductRow code never worked -- ignore it.

ACCEPTANCE -- four live checks by the human on localhost:3000:

  AC1  Images never pop. Every product image eases blur -> sharp via the
       reveal mechanism from `sang-logium-7j8`; no single-frame snap, no
       synchronized wall, no hydration-gated collapse.

  AC2  Streaming is resilient on Back / Forward (browser arrows). Products
       still arrive in gradual row-by-row chunks, not one wall; images still
       reveal and are never stuck in blur / hidden.

  AC3  Same holds on soft navigation (Next.js client nav, not a hard reload)
       AND on every grid route -- /products, /products/headphones,
       /products/accessories, any category slug. It "just works" everywhere.

  AC4  Cache-resilient. With the Next cache warm, the grid just works:
       streaming happens only if there is still work to stream (likely
       instant from cache), and images are never stuck in a blurred / hidden
       state because of the reveal mechanism on a cached render.

Current status: Not started. Blocked on `sang-logium-p0g` and `sang-logium-7j8`.
notes:
RISK ASSESSMENT (added 2026-08-30)

== A. OUTCOME RISKS (wrong result, mix-up, hallucination, quality drop) ==

A1. Reinventing a mechanism that already exists. This issue is the resilience
    umbrella, not a new reveal/streaming design. Risk: an agent rebuilds the
    reveal or streaming path and re-pops.
    MITIGATE: consume `sang-logium-p0g` / `sang-logium-7j8` output as-is; only
    add what makes them survive nav + cache. If either upstream isn't landed,
    stop -- this is blocked-by both.

A2. Losing streaming OR reveal under Back/Forward. bfcache / RSC cache restore
    can replay a finished tree so the reveal script never re-fires, leaving
    images stuck blurred; or gate visibility so all rows flip at once.
    MITIGATE: reveal must be idempotent on restore (check img.complete on
    mount/pageshow, mark shown without a transition when already painted).
    Never gate row/image opacity on hydration (AI_LESSONS L02 / the 7j8 F.1
    failure).

A3. Route coverage assumed, not checked. Fixing /products/headphones and
    assuming /products/accessories and bare /products behave identically.
    MITIGATE: the human live-checks at least /products, one category, and one
    more category slug. Agent states which routes it reasoned about, not that
    all pass.

A4. Cache path never actually exercised. "Cache-resilient" claimed from
    reading code, not from a warm-cache render.
    MITIGATE: describe the cached-render reasoning and the sibling it mirrors;
    hand the warm-cache verdict to the human. Do not assert AC4 passes.

A5. Height / layout regression. ChunkedProductGrid / ProductCard /
    ProductImage are under the CLAUDE.md height-sizing review gate.
    MITIGATE: minimal diff to those files; run the h- / aspect- / min-h- diff
    review before hand-off even if not asked.

A6. isOpaque LQIP gate dropped on the real data. POC gates the underlay on
    metadata.isOpaque; applying it to transparent PNGs looks wrong.
    MITIGATE: carry the gate across; confirm the real product query exposes
    isOpaque.

A7. False "it feels resilient" pass. Perceptible reveal, "arrives in chunks",
    "not a wall" are all human-eye judgements on :3000.
    MITIGATE: agent lists what changed and which POC behaviour it mirrors;
    the four ACs are the human's verdict.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS (agent adds fat instead of the lean path) ==

Lean path = small edits wiring the two proven pieces into the real grid so
they survive nav + cache, then hand off. Human runs the four AC live checks
on :3000.

B1. No build / tsc / ts-check / lint / test runs.
B2. No agent-run dev server, no browser automation, no Lighthouse/crawl for
    verification (AI_LESSONS L04). If a bfcache / RSC-restore timing question
    is genuinely in doubt, build a throwaway single-file HTML harness (L05),
    not an in-app check.
B3. No new dependency, no config change.
B4. Do not touch app/(test)/streaming-poc/ -- it stays as the reference.
B5. No new docs -- the trail is _project/audits/streaming-poc/. One Attempt
    entry there only if a genuinely new approach is tried.
B6. No subagents. No git (no branch/commit/push).
B7. Minimal diff; new files over edits where possible; don't reformat
    untouched code.

Expected footprint: small edits to the real grid + reveal wiring
(ChunkedProductGrid / ProductImage and the ported reveal script/CSS), plus
whatever makes the reveal idempotent on bf/RSC restore. No deps / config /
tooling changes. If the diff is well past this, it's over-building -- stop.

== C. EXECUTION MODEL ==

Recommend Claude Sonnet (claude-sonnet-5).
Rationale: this is bounded wiring of two already-proven pieces against a
tight lean-path spec and a fixed reference (streaming-poc), not novel
architecture -- Sonnet covers the cross-file reasoning (hydration, bfcache,
the h-/aspect gate) at the lowest cost that is still safe. Opus adds cost and
tends to over-build here, which the guardrails already fight. Haiku is too
light for the hydration/cache subtlety and the height-sizing review gate.

IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-30) — resilience wiring only, no new mechanism.

- app/components/features/products/ImageRevealClient.tsx (NEW, "use client", renders null)
- ImageRevealScript.tsx: export REVEAL_SCRIPT, add `instant` flag to scan/reveal, expose window.__slImageRevealScan, wrap MutationObserver/DOMContentLoaded/load callers
- reveal.module.css: + .reveal[data-instant]{transition:none}
- ChunkedProductGrid.tsx: render <ImageRevealClient/> beside <ImageRevealScript/>

Covers: soft nav from non-grid first page (inline <script> won't re-exec on client
render -> client companion injects it once, guarded); Back/Forward via pageshow
persisted -> instant (transition-free) reveal of already-painted images; route
coverage is structural (both /products and /products/[...slug] go through
ChunkedProductGrid). isOpaque LQIP gate confirmed live (getProductsByVfsKeys L50).

First-view eased reveal (7j8) path untouched. No deps/config. POC untouched.
h-/aspect-/min-h- review gate: no sizing classNames changed.

title: [Filters] Active-filter chips + Clear all <-> URL
description:
SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY: This control's only responsibility: (a) on user interaction, write the correct value to the URL via nuqs; (b) on URL change - including first load, deep link, and browser back/forward - render its own display to match the URL. It does not know about, import, query, or react to the product grid, product data, result counts, or streaming. It reads the same shared param contract from F1 that F2-F5 write.

ACCEPTANCE TESTS - human live check on the dev server at localhost:3000, watching the address bar, starting from a URL that already has several filter + sort params set, on /products/headphones and /products:

Happy path
- When I load a URL with brand, price and sort params set, then I see one chip per active value, with price shown as a single range chip.
- When I click the X on a brand chip, then that value leaves the brand param in the address bar and the chip disappears; other chips and params stay.
- When I click "Clear all", then every filter and sort param is removed from the address bar in a single step, and all chips disappear.
- When there are no active filters, then the chip row and "Clear all" are absent (or "Clear all" is disabled).
- When I remove a chip, then the page does not do a full white reload.

Edge path
- When I click "Clear all" while a search query param is also in the URL, then that query param stays and only the filter/sort params are removed.
- When I press Back right after "Clear all", then all the previous filters and their chips come back in lockstep with the address bar.
- When a param in the URL holds a value with no matching label, then its chip shows the raw value cleanly or is omitted - never a broken or blank chip.
- When price is set to only one bound, then the range chip reads sensibly (e.g. "From $X" or "Up to $Y").

OUT OF SCOPE
- Whether the product grid actually updates when a chip is removed.
- Visual styling (V1), mobile (V2), keyboard and screen-reader behaviour.

RISK ASSESSMENT

Outcome risks (wrong result / mix-up / hallucination / false positive)
- Chips deriving state from a local mirror that drifts from the URL. Mitigation: chips are a pure render of F1's parsed URL state; the only write path is F1's setters.
- "Clear all" nuking unrelated params - ?q= (search), ?page= (pagination). Mitigation: clear only the explicit F1 filter/sort key list; the "?q= survives Clear all" test is the gate.
- "Clear all" producing one history entry per param, so Back needs many presses to undo. Mitigation: a single batched setter call (useQueryStates / F1 serializer) => one history entry.
- Inventing display labels for values. The human-readable labels come from the same option lists F5 receives as props. Mitigation: F6 takes a label-resolver prop; raw-value fallback; never a blank chip.
- Price rendered as two separate chips, or a one-sided range reading wrong. Mitigation: explicit range-chip rule ("$X-$Y", "From $X", "Up to $Y") - one chip for the pair.
- Building F6 before F2-F5 exist and guessing their param keys. Mitigation: F6 is sequenced last; every key and parser is imported from F1.
- Reacting to the grid / result count (e.g. "Clear all" only when results are empty). Mitigation: SRP - URL in, URL out.

Execution risks (unnecessary work / time cost)
- tsc / ts-check / build / lint / tests / npm install. Mitigation: none - forbidden; inspection only.
- Agent-run dev server or browser automation. Mitigation: the human does the :3000 address-bar check.
- A chip / tag UI library. Mitigation: small static markup styled with V1's tokens; zero new deps.
- Also wiring the grid to prove removal re-queries. Mitigation: out of scope; ends at the URL.
- No new docs; no commit/push unless asked.

Expected footprint: one client component that reads all F1 params, maps them to chips with a label resolver, and calls per-key clear + a batched clear-all from F1. No dependency or config changes.

SEQUENCE: After F1, V1, and F2-F5.

CURRENT STATUS: Not started.
notes:
RISK ASSESSMENT (added 2026-08-30)

== A. OUTCOME RISKS (wrong result, mix-up, hallucination, quality drop) ==

A1. Control reaches past its one job (URL <-> own display).
    Importing / querying / reacting to the product grid, product data, result counts, or streaming.
    MITIGATE: inputs are the F1 params (the same ones F2-F5 write) + whatever label lookup is
    passed as props. If it needs the grid, the boundary is wrong - stop and flag.

A2. Reimplementing the param contract instead of reading F1.
    F6 must READ the exact params F2-F5 write, via F1's parsers.
    MITIGATE: import F1; no bespoke URL parsing; stay in sync if F2-F5's shapes change.

A3. "Clear all" scope wrong.
    Must remove every filter + sort param in ONE step but LEAVE unrelated params (e.g. ?q= search)
    intact.
    MITIGATE: clear exactly the F1-owned keys; merge, don't replace, the query.

A4. Chip rendering edge cases (the edge paths ARE the spec).
    One chip per active value; price as a single range chip; single-bound price reads sensibly
    ("From $X" / "Up to $Y"); a value with no matching label shows the raw value cleanly or is
    omitted - never blank/broken; no chip row and no "Clear all" (or disabled) when nothing is
    active; Back after "Clear all" restores all chips in lockstep.
    MITIGATE: work the Edge-path list item by item.

A5. Full white reload on chip removal.
    MITIGATE: soft URL update via the nuqs setter; chips derive from the URL.

A6. Scope bleed into styling (V1), mobile (V2), a11y, or a sibling F-issue.
    MITIGATE: behaviour only; reuse V1 chip markup; F6 is last - don't pre-empt F2-F5.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS (agent adds fat instead of the lean path) ==

Lean path = wire the chip row + Clear all to the URL, hand off. Human watches the address bar on :3000.

B1. No build / tsc / lint / test runs.
B2. No agent-run dev server or browser automation.
B3. nuqs already present - no npm install.
B4. Don't rebuild V1 chip markup - import / extend it.
B5. Don't re-derive the F1 contract or F2-F5's param shapes - import them.
B6. No new docs, no long analysis, no subagents.
B7. Ignore git - no commits.

Expected footprint: 1 component reading F1's params + a label-map prop. No deps / config.

title: [Sorting] Sort dropdown <-> URL
description:

- When I paste a URL that already contains a sort param (e.g. sort = newest) and load it, then the sort control shows "Newest" selected on arrival.

title: [Streaming] Product images pop in instead of revealing
description:
Goal: On the streaming POC page, each product image must visibly ease from its LQIP blur placeholder to the full sharp image over a short, gentle transition that the end user can actually perceive. Right now images snap into view in a single frame the moment their download completes - no visible blur-to-sharp reveal - so the grid still feels abrupt, jittery, and mechanical instead of resolving like a calm wave. The existing spoc-image-in CSS fade (opacity 0.35->1 + blur 8px->0, 320ms) is either not firing or is imperceptible; the fix must make the gradual reveal genuinely visible while keeping criteria 2 (top-to-bottom load order) and 3 (uniform motion, no stagger) from sang-logium-7ao intact and staying server-only (no client component, per LESSONS L02).

Hard constraints:

* solution cannot interfere with solution of streaming ux: products appearing faster in smaller chunks, instead of taking longer and appearing all at once as one big wall

Current status: Attempt G on working tree - the professional, ship-able solution. A small "use client" RevealImage wrapper (the standard next/image reveal, same as Vercel's commerce template): onLoad -> setState -> class, state also seeded from a ref callback checking img.complete so priority/cached images reveal at once. It renders the .spoc-lqip placeholder while !loaded and unmounts it on load (one commit, exactly what next/image's own placeholder="blur" does).

Key to not regressing the 7ao streaming: .spoc-reveal is BLUR ONLY, no opacity. The image is opacity:1 the frame its bytes paint - hydration-independent - so products still stream in as fast small chunks. Hydration only governs when the blur eases off (450ms, 320ms reduced-motion). F.1 failed here because it used opacity:0 gated on client state, so images stayed invisible until their leaf hydrated and then flipped in a burst = one wall, later.

No hydration mismatch (useState(false) identical both sides; class change is a normal post-hydration update). No inline script, no MutationObserver, no data-* attribute hack, no suppressHydrationWarning, no timed node removal - all of which the earlier F.2/F.3 script approach needed.

Files: app/(test)/streaming-poc/RevealImage.tsx (new), page.tsx, app/globals.css. Full log incl. superseded attempts A-F: _project/audits/streaming-poc/failed-attempts.md (Attempt G). Pending: human sign-off on :3000 - reveal visible, console clean, rows 1/2/3 flush independently under throttling.

title: [Streaming] Calm deliberate product image arrival
description:
Goal: On the streaming POC page, make the moment product images arrive feel calm and deliberate instead of abrupt and random. Judged against three criteria only:

1. Blur-to-sharp, not blank-to-pop — each image visibly eases from its LQIP blur placeholder to the full image via a short, gentle transition; it never snaps in from nothing.

3. Calm, uniform motion — every image uses the exact same transition style and duration; no two images side by side fading at different speeds, no staggered flashing.
